item.title: Tinubu’s reforms favour rich, worsen poverty — Atedo Peterside
item.description: Atedo Peterside, founder of Stanbic IBTC Bank Plc and Anap Foundation, has said President Bola Tinubu’s economic reforms have benefited wealthy Nigerians while worsening the living conditions of millions of low-income earners. Peterside stated this on Monday during an interview on Arise Television, arguing that although upper-middle-class Nigerians had recorded improvements in their investments and incomes over the past three years, poorer households were struggling to afford basic necessities. He said the reforms had not adequately addressed the economic difficulties confronting the majority of Nigerians. “If you’re upper middle class, I can probably show on the blackboard investments in the stock exchange and all that stuff. “I can show on the blackboard that you’re probably better off in the last three years. If you’re a low-income worker, like somebody without much savings and struggling to eat — what 100 million Nigerians have to do, to eat two meals a day and struggling to pay your bills, I can show you that you’re a lot worse off,” he said. Peterside faulted the government for failing to establish adequate social safety nets for poor Nigerians while implementing the reforms. Citing 2025 data from TheCable Index, he said poverty levels varied significantly across the country’s geopolitical zones, with the North-West, North-East, North-Central and South-South bearing a heavy burden. He said only about 12 states and the Federal Capital Territory had poverty rates below 50 per cent. According to him, most of the states with poverty rates below that threshold were in the South-West, alongside Anambra in the South-East and Edo and Delta in the South-South. Peterside said the regional disparities could shape how Nigerians assess the impact of the government’s economic policies. He added that policymakers might not fully appreciate the depth of poverty in some parts of the country because they did not frequently visit affected communities. “High poverty in Nigeria is largely a zonal problem. It is a problem of the North-West, of the North-East, of the North-Central, and of the South-South,” he said. The businessman maintained that the absence of adequate social protection for vulnerable Nigerians remained a major gap in the implementation of the government’s economic reforms. Vanguard Newspaper The post Tinubu’s reforms favour rich, worsen poverty — Atedo Peterside appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: The Elder Scroll 6: Sentinel's Name Quietly Teases Juicy 'Skyrim' Sequel
item.description: Eight years after the original announcement , we've finally learned the name of Bethesda's next RPG: The Elder Scrolls 6: Sentinel . Since the developer didn't show any gameplay footage, all fans can really do is muse on the meaning of the title. As disappointing as that is, Elder Scrolls loreheads do have plenty to chew on.

item.title: Sultan a beacon of unity, stability, says Lawal
item.description: Zamfara State Governor Dauda Lawal has described the Sultan of Sokoto, Alhaji Muhammad Sa’ad Abubakar III, as a unifying leader whose wisdom and steady leadership promote stability. Lawal stated this on Monday at the 13th Shaikh Usmanu Bin Fodiyo Week and the 20th anniversary of the Sultan’s coronation, held at the International Conference Centre, Sokoto. The event, themed, ‘Reviving Ethical Leadership and Social Harmony: Lessons from Sokoto Jihad Leaders’, attracted prominent personalities from Nigeria and beyond. In his goodwill message, the governor said the government and people of Zamfara State had drawn inspiration from the Sultan’s wisdom, guidance and leadership, particularly during challenging social and security situations. Lawal congratulated the Sultan on the 20th anniversary of his coronation, describing it as a historic milestone. He also expressed appreciation for the Sultan’s recent presence and support during the coronation and presentation of staff of office to 19 emirs in Gusau, saying it demonstrated his commitment to strengthening traditional institutions in the region. The governor said the legacy of the Sokoto Caliphate transcended geographical boundaries, noting that its values of knowledge, justice, moral discipline, responsible leadership and human dignity remained relevant to contemporary challenges. He urged Nigerians, particularly residents of Zamfara, to draw lessons from the teachings of Sheikh Usmanu Dan Fodiyo in addressing insecurity, poverty, moral decline and youth vulnerability. Lawal called for greater emphasis on peace, justice, education and social responsibility to strengthen communities. Earlier, the Sultan thanked individuals and groups who had supported him during his 20 years on the throne. He also urged religious, traditional and community leaders to intensify efforts towards promoting peace. The post Sultan a beacon of unity, stability, says Lawal appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Up 53 spots! Vaishnavi Sharma makes giant leap in ICC ODI rankings after stunning spells against Zimbabwe
item.description: NEW DELHI: India's 3-0 clean sweep against Zimbabwe in the three-match ODI series has brought several players into the spotlight in the latest ICC Women's ODI Player Rankings, with young spinner Vaishnavi Sharma making the biggest jump after an impressive performance in the series finale. The 20-year-old left-arm spinner climbed an impressive 53 places to reach 94th in the ODI bowling rankings after claiming nine wickets across the second and third matches of the series. It was a remarkable rise for Vaishnavi, who has made an immediate impact in just her first three appearances in the format. After picking up four wickets in the second ODI, Vaishnavi delivered a match-winning performance in the series finale, returning figures of 5/39. Her maiden five-wicket haul in ODIs earned her the Player of the Match award as India completed a comprehensive series sweep in the ICC Women's Championship. Sayali Satghare, Kranti Gaud also rise Vaishnavi was not the only Indian bowler to benefit from the series against Zimbabwe. Sayali Satghare climbed 18 places to 85th in the latest bowling rankings following an impressive outing in the third ODI. The right-arm pacer returned figures of 2/11 from six overs, including 30 dot balls, underlining her effectiveness with the new ball. Kranti Gaud also made progress, moving up one place to 24th after claiming two wickets in Vadodara. Zimbabwe's Nomvelo Sibanda gained two places to reach 60th in the bowling rankings. She made an early impact in the final ODI, dismissing Yastika Bhatia off the first ball of India's innings. Pratika Rawal, Shafali Verma make batting gains There were positive developments for Indian batters as well, with Pratika Rawal continuing her consistent run in the series. The opener climbed three places to 18th after registering her third consecutive half-century against Zimbabwe. Shafali Verma also moved up eight places to joint 65th following her attacking 51-run knock in the series finale. Zimbabwe's batters made progress in the latest update too. Opener Modester Mupachikwa climbed three places to 36th after scoring 37 in the third ODI, while captain Josephine Nkomo gained two spots to reach 49th.

item.title: Un punto más para el Barça en la Youth League (3-3)
item.description: Un punto más para el Barça en la Youth League (3-3) El conjunto azulgrana consigue sumar un punto ante el Aston Villa para escalar posiciones en la clasificación de la UEFA Youth League. El Barça se ha enfrentado ante el Aston Villa (3-3) en la cuarta jornada de la fase de liga de la UEFA Youth League . El conjunto azulgrana necesitaba sumar puntos para acercarse a lo alto de la clasificación y evitar la eliminatoria previa a los octavos de final. Tras un partido lleno de intensidad e intentos, han conseguido igualar el marcador gracias a un gol de Iu Martínez en los últimos instantes del encuentro. Los de Pol Planas tienen dos jornadas más por delante para conseguir su objetivo, ante el Sabah y el Manchester City . El Barça ante el Aston Villa en la Youth League / Sergio Sorolla / @foto.monjo Llegan los refuerzos El Barça salía con todo ante un partido importante con la necesidad de sumar los tres puntos . Pol Planas aprovechó la presencia de Ebrima Tunkara y Hamza Abdelkarim , jugadores con dinámica del primer equipo para echarles una mano desde el inicio del partido. El técnico apostó por un once inicial de gala para reencontrarse con la victoria en Europa tras el empate ante el PSG . El Barça empezó manteniendo el balón con buenas asociaciones y amplia creatividad para atacar los espacios. Los azulgranas se encontraron con un planteamiento conocido, un rival con falta de ideas sin intención de apretar. Ebrima Tunkara no tardó mucho en demostrar porque habían contado con él para este encuentro. El futbolista azulgrana remató de cabeza con suerte para aprovechar el rechace y abrir el marcador (1-0). El Aston Villa se vio obligado a reaccionar lo antes posible. El conjunto de James Shan se puso las pilas para tener un par de ocasiones de peligro y acercarse al área rival, pero Bonfill y Baba no cedieron. El conjunto azulgrana se sentía cómodo pero tenía hambre. Tras una buena recuperación, iniciaron un contragolpe efectivo superando rápidamente las zonas del campo hasta que Tunkara encontró a Joni Hernández para ampliar la ventaja en el marcador (2-0). El Aston Villa despertó tarde. El conjunto inglés apretaba con tanta fuerza en el tramo final de la primer mitad que pudo lograr igualar el marcador con dos saques de esquina (2-2). Los adversarios recortaron la distancia para dirigirse al descanso un poco más aliviados. Sin embargo, una perspectiva muy diferente a los azulgranas que se marchaban encajando dos goles en cuestión de diez minutos. Cuesta arriba Giro de 180 grados. Parecía que el Barça tenía las de ganar, pero debían seguir remando. Los azulgranas no agacharon la cabeza, salieron con ganas de llevarse la victoria y con buena presión ofensiva tras la entrada de Gistau y Mirangels . El conjunto azulgrana quería recuperar las sensaciones iniciales para volver a estar cómodos. La interesante lucha de Tunkara en todos los balones demostraba la mentalidad del equipo: querían ganar. N o se daban por vencidos, querían más y necesitaban más. E

item.title: Falcons Cut Drake Jackson And Jared Ivey Ahead Of Week 9
item.description: Dale Zanine-Imagn Images The Atlanta Falcons made a quick roster shakeup on Monday afternoon. The team released outside linebacker Jared Ivey and defensive end Drake Jackson just as Week 9 gets ready to start. This move comes right after a rough 16-0 loss to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Sunday. The team needs fresh legs to handle the Cincinnati Bengals next Sunday. Per the Atlanta Falcons official report, both players are gone from the 53-man roster effective immediately. Ivey played 17 snaps on Sunday but did not record a single stat. He had been on the roster since the team claimed him off waivers in late August. According to the Atlanta Falcons, he appeared in seven games this season with one sack and two tackles for a loss. He started his career with the Seattle Seahawks and was part of their Super Bowl win in 2025. That title makes his release even more surprising for fans who liked his energy. The team let him go despite his recent playing time and past success. Why the defense needs a spark Drake Jackson played 20 snaps over two games before he got cut. He joined the roster on October 24 after spending last year with the Washington Commanders. Per Heavy.com , he was inactive for the game against Tampa Bay on Sunday. His time in Atlanta was short and unproductive. Although he was selected in the second round from USC, staying healthy has proven difficult for him. Injuries and poor play have hurt his career since he was drafted by the 49ers in 2022. The Falcons are clearly looking for someone else to fill the pass-rush role. The timing of this move points to a specific plan. According to The Falcoholic , James Pearce Jr. is eligible to return from suspension this week. Yasir Abdullah can also come back from injured reserve. These two players offer the speed and run defense the team needs against Joe Burrow. The Falcons likely need the roster spots for these returns. It makes sense to clear the bench for players who have already proven they can play in this system. The Falcons will try to bring Ivey and Jackson back on the practice squad. Heavy.com notes that Ivey is a Super Bowl champion who might land there quickly. Jackson has the pedigree to get another shot too. The team wants to keep them close in case they need depth later. This is a common move for the NFL when teams need to make room for returning stars. It keeps the talent in the building without using a 53-man spot. The defense must fix its run issues before Sunday. The team allowed 16 points and no offense against the Buccaneers. A better pass rush is the only way to stop the Bengals offense.

item.title: Iraola urges Liverpool to 'kill' Fenerbahce's hostile atmosphere
item.description: Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola (BERK OZKAN) Andoni Iraola has urged Liverpool to stop Fenerbahce in Wednesday's Champions League clash by killing the hostile atmosphere generated by their raucous fans. Iraola is expecting a deafening atmosphere at the Sukru Saracoglu stadium in Istanbul, but the Liverpool boss is confident his side can cope with the unwelcoming environment. The Spaniard believes Liverpool must cut off the connection between Fenerbahce's players and their passionate fans by taking the sting out of the game. "Tomorrow, it's not going to be easy. It's always difficult to come to Turkey and play and we have to be very ready," Iraola said on Tuesday. "They have experienced players who know how to play in this competition. We have to try to kill the confidence and momentum they can have with the supporters. "Champions League away days are difficult and we know this, especially in this stadium and atmosphere. We have to be mentally very ready. "We want to continue how we have done in the Champions League. It is a good chance to get to 12 points and then finish in the top eight." Stopping Fenerbahce's momentum in such a febrile atmosphere might be easier said than done for Liverpool. In Sunday's 1-0 defeat against Premier League champions Arsenal, Liverpool failed to register a shot on target in a home league game for the first time since records began in 2003. That lack of cutting edge has been an issue at times for Liverpool this season as they adapt to Iraola's preferred style of play. But their 100 per cent Champions League record this season has seen them score six against LASK, four against Villarreal and two against Atletico Madrid, compared to 11 in nine Premier League matches. Asked if he had learnt from Liverpool's impotence against Arsenal, Iraola added: "It is difficult when you lose but honestly I am happy with a lot of things from the other day. "I liked a lot of things but we still need to improve, especially attacking the box. "A lot of times we were there with the numbers but not making the proper runs and waiting for second balls. "We put Arsenal under pressure and they defended well but I liked a lot of things." Fifth-placed Liverpool are already nine points behind leaders Arsenal in the title race. It is hardly the start Iraola would have been hoping for in his first season since arriving from Bournemouth to replace the sacked Arne Slot. "I think we have had better results in the Champions League and Carabao Cup but it's very early in the season to establish comparisons," Iraola said. Liverpool will be without Dutch midfielder Ryan Gravenberch, who was left at home after reporting discomfort with a heel problem during the warm-up on Sunday. smg/iwd

item.title: Gopher Women Defeat Harvard 82-62
item.description: There are a lot of new faces that the #17/18 Minnesota Golden Gophers are breaking into their lineup for the 2026-27 season. For the first three quarters of Monday’s season opener against Harvard, it definitely looked like a team that had not spent a ton of time playing together. But the Gophers took over and put together a complete final quarter to extend a two point lead after three quarters into a 20 point 82-62 win to open the season 1-0. Minnesota picked up three new players in the transfer portal and had a pair of impact freshmen that were all supposed to make an impact this season, and from game one we saw just that. All three transfers and both impact freshman played at least 14 minutes in the win over the Crimson led by Natalie Kussow’s 32 minutes. Kussow was in the Gophers starting lineup filling the void left by the injury to Tori McKinney and was joined by the expected pair of Mara Braun and Grace Grocholski along with a pair of transfers in Leah Harmon and Tayla Thomas. While Penn State center transfer Gracie Merkle did not start, she made the most of her 18 minutes off the bench leading the Gophers with 22 points. Minnesota and Harvard were locked in a back and forth battle for the first three quarters. Minnesota’s largest lead in the opening ten minutes was just four points as the Crimson kept close, and Minnesota struggled to shoot the long ball. In fact Minnesota did not make a three pointer until Grace Grocholski hit one with 4:06 left in the second quarter to put the Gophers up 28-25. A pair of Merkle layups gave the Gophers their largest lead of the game at that point of eight points, and a Harvard free throw would cut the lead to seven at halftime with Minnesota leading 37-30. Harvard came out the aggressors right away in the third quarter. A quick 7-0 aided by five Minnesota turnovers tied the game. Minnesota did score their first basket of the second half until nearly four minutes into the third quarter. They then went on a 7-0 run of their own to take a seven point lead once more, but Harvard came storming back taking a lead of their own late in the quarter. It would take a Grocholski three with six seconds left in the third to put Minnesota back on top 54-52 headed into the final ten minutes. There the Gophers finally played up to their capabilities. They clamped down on defense and started taking the ball to the basket and getting open looks. Minnesota opened the quarter on a 21-4 run and never looked back. Coach P emptied the bench with a minute left in the game getting Kylee Pabin and Adit Kuol their first action in a Gopher uniform and Minnesota opened the season with a 82-62 win. To steal from Blake, and with accounts that this is the first game of the year, we have our own Elite, Meh, and Ugly from Minnesota’s win: Elite: As Grace and Gracie go, so will the Gophers. It was the G & G show for Minnesota last night as Merkle made her Minnesota debut and did exactly what was expected scoring a team high 22 points in 18

item.title: MLB Mariners hire 36-year-old Kanzler as new manager
item.description: Jason Kanzler has been named the new manager of Major League Baseball's Seattle Mariners (Michael Reaves) Jason Kanzler, player development director for the Chicago Cubs over the past three seasons, has been hired as manager of the Seattle Mariners, the Major League Baseball club announced Tuesday. Kanzler, in his first managerial post, becomes the 22nd manager in Mariners history and at age 36 is the second-youngest manager in MLB after Washington's 34-year-old Blake Butera. "Our goal in this process was finding a manager with the ability to challenge all of us to improve," Mariners president of baseball operations Jerry Dipoto said. "Jason has the mindset, expertise, communication skills, and intensity to help create a championship standard here in Seattle." Kanzler replaced Dan Wilson, who was dropped at the end of this year's campaign after just over two seasons with the Mariners in which he went 187-171. Seattle won the American League West division last year with a record of 90-72, but slid to 76-86 this year, settling for third in the division. "I'm thrilled to join the Mariners organization and I'm looking forward to hitting the ground running," Kanzler said. "This team has an immense amount of talent in all facets of the game and my coaching staff and I are excited to access and unlock this team's full potential." Kanzler served as an assistant coach for the Houston Astros in 2022 when they won the World Series and in 2023 before joining the Cubs. js/amz

item.title: The Low Block, Week 11: Ashes
item.description: I am going to start this week’s entry by talking about Dominic Pereira. I gave him a huge amount of flak in the early parts of this season. I repeatedly said that he struggles with claiming crosses and dominating his penalty area. That wasn’t a wrong observation, but I mentioned it basically every week for the first month of this column. When both Pereira and Geno Cervoni were having lackluster performances, I said that Russell Payne had a “goalkeeper crisis” on his hands. I essentially blamed the Sophomore for most of the goals NU conceded up until about the Xavier game. Pereira has, since that initial start, been stellar in between the sticks for Northwestern this season. For all of this team’s defensive woes throughout the season, it boasts the third-best defense in conference play while Pereira is top five in save percentage. Against Ohio State, Pereira made a number of incredible saves to keep NU alive in its push for an equalizer. I’m going to do a “top five players of the season” in the final issue of this column (to make up for going away from the weekly top fives), make no mistake his name will likely be in that top five. He’s been at an extremely high level for a long time now, and I just wanted to start out this week’s column by giving credit where credit is due. In other words, the season is over. A loss at Ohio State means that the Wildcats are mathematically eliminated from the Big Ten Tournament with one game left to play in the conference slate. A draw would have given NU a fighting chance going into the Wisconsin matchup; it would have been a must-win game and then the ‘Cats would’ve had to pray that UCLA loses to Washington — though, it wouldn’t have been too far-fetched to expect that UCLA loss. But, NU played itself out of the chance. And it didn’t happen just this week, although this outing was rather emblematic. The ’Cats gained four points from three games against the three teams below them in the conference and played two of those games with 10 men. You have to take the points when they are offered. It’s never smart to deal in hypotheticals, but if NU managed to beat Penn State (which never should have been that tall of a task) and managed to convert one of its 2.16 expected goals worth of chances against UCLA, its destiny would be in its own hands right now. But slim margins produce big ramifications. Maybe NU can play spoiler to the Badgers’ tournament hopes. Going about this week’s column is weird, there’s nothing to really look forward to anymore as far as this season is concerned, but I also want to hold off on reflecting on the last issue of the column. I’ll try and find a happy medium by looking forward to next season a little. This team is going to lose 10 players to graduation next year. Four of those 10 (Andrew Millar, Peter Reisz, Fritz Volmar, Bryant Mayer) were nailed on week-in-week-out starters, while four others were regular contributors (Tyler Glassberg, Marco Silva, Baraka Tarleton, Yuval Nimrodi). item.title: Alli vows to surpass Makinde’s eight-year record in four years
item.description: APC candidate unveils ‘Oyo AHEAD’ development blueprint By Adeola Badru The governorship candidate of the All Progressives Congress (APC) in Oyo State, Sharafadeen Abiodun Alli, has pledged to surpass the achievements of Governor Seyi Makinde’s eight-year administration within four years if elected in 2027. Alli made the promise on Tuesday during the unveiling of his manifesto, tagged ‘Oyo AHEAD’ (Itayo Oyo), at Theophilus Ogunlesi Hall, opposite the University College Hospital, Ibadan. He said the blueprint was designed to reposition the state through purposeful leadership, strategic planning, stronger institutions and people-oriented governance. The APC candidate said Oyo State had enormous economic and developmental potential that could be harnessed through deliberate policies and innovative approaches to improve the lives of residents. He said his ambition was to build a state where opportunities would be accessible to all, public institutions strengthened and the impact of government policies felt across communities, irrespective of their location or socio-economic circumstances. “Oyo State has enormous potential, but we must be deliberate, innovative and committed to translating that potential into tangible improvements in the lives of our people,” he said. Alli described Oyo AHEAD as more than a campaign slogan, saying it represented a comprehensive development agenda based on the expectations of residents and the need to accelerate the state’s development. “Oyo AHEAD is not just a campaign slogan; it represents a development agenda anchored on the people’s expectations and the urgent need to move our state forward. “We want an Oyo State that works for everyone, regardless of location, background or economic status,” he said. He said sustainable development required a coordinated strategy to strengthen institutions, stimulate productive sectors, expand economic opportunities and ensure inclusive participation in governance. “Sustainable development cannot be achieved through isolated interventions. We must strengthen our institutions, support productive sectors, create opportunities for our young people and ensure that every segment of society has a stake in the development process,” he added. The APC candidate said restoring Oyo State’s position among Nigeria’s leading states would require purposeful leadership, responsible governance and a development approach that placed residents’ welfare at the centre of government decisions. He said the manifesto contained policies, programmes and strategies to address the state’s development challenges across various sectors. Alli expressed confidence that his proposed four-year administration would deliver measurable results and surpass the achievements of the incumbent government over its eight-year tenure. item.title: Tyreek Hill’s Return To Chiefs Looks Dead After New Report
item.description: Rich Storry-Imagn Images Forget the dream of seeing Tyreek Hill in red and gold again. The path for him to play for the Kansas City Chiefs this season has effectively vanished. A recent civil jury verdict found Hill liable for two counts related to domestic violence, which complicates any potential move. On top of that, he is still rehabbing from multiple torn knee ligaments, a fact confirmed by RotoBaller. The timing is brutal. The calendar has flipped to November, which is long past the October return goal his agent, Drew Rosenhaus, had previously set. The Injury and Legal Double Whammy A nasty injury cut short Hill’s 2025 season. Now, at 31 years old, he has not signed with any NFL team. RotoBaller notes that fantasy managers should look elsewhere for help because of these issues. The legal trouble adds a massive layer of risk that no franchise wants to handle. Heavy.com reported that the jury verdict came down in a confusing civil case. The combination of a torn knee and a court finding of liability creates a wall that is nearly impossible to climb over. Chiefs Already Have Their Answers Even if Hill were healthy and cleared legally, the Chiefs do not need him. They already have young talent sitting on the roster who are not playing to their potential. ESPN’s Dan Graziano wrote a blunt assessment of the situation. “I know we do this all the time with the Chiefs, but they have guys. They just aren’t playing to their potential. Rashee Rice was a second-round pick. Xavier Worthy was a first-round pick! Remember how mad everybody got at the Bills for letting the Chiefs move up to take him? Guys like that are supposed to be the solutions.” Graziano points out that the team has high draft picks who should be the fix. Heavy.com notes that the Chiefs prefer using these existing players over signing a free agent. The logic is sound. Why bring in a 31-year-old with a bad knee and legal baggage when you have first-round picks waiting to step up? The front office knows this. They are looking at the trade deadline, but they are not looking at Hill. A Cold Reality for Fans The idea that Hill returns to Arrowhead is a story fans want to tell themselves, but the facts do not support it. He is not on a roster, he is injured, and he is facing serious legal scrutiny. The Chiefs have a game against the New York Jets on Sunday, Nov. 8. They will face that challenge with their current squad. The days of waiting for the former Miami Dolphins star to come home are over.

item.title: The transplanted Scot doing famous father proud in New Zealand
item.description: Clark Laidlaw has been head coach at Super Rugby champions Hurricanes for three seasons [Getty Images] A few weeks back, four Scots shot the breeze in New Zealand, a meeting of rugby intellects transplanted from Edinburgh, Inverness, Yetholm and Jedburgh - all of them doing great things in their adopted land. Mike Blair was one of them. On Saturday, in what promises to be a surreal day for him, the former Scotland captain will return to Murrayfield as attack coach for the All Blacks. Euan Mackintosh was another. Mackintosh is the All Blacks' skills acquisition coach. The third man was Adam Hay, who is New Zealand's performance scientist. The fourth was Clark Laidlaw, son of the great Roy, cousin of Greig and Super Rugby champion coach in 2026. "We were getting a bit of stick at lunch, the four of us talking Scottish," says Laidlaw, whose Hurricanes team not only won Super Rugby in late June, they dominated it. Finishing top of the table when the regular season ended, they won their first knockout game 66-12 against the Brumbies, then beat the Blues 57-21 in the semi-final before dismantling the Chiefs 60-5 in the final. It was Laidlaw's third season in charge. He's far more celebrated in New Zealand than he is at home. He's been there for 18 years, on and off, and he spoke about his life and times on the BBC's Scotland Rugby Podcast , how he went from a school-leaver at 16 to a New Zealand sevens coach - Commonwealth Games gold, World Cup Sevens gold, Olympics silver in Tokyo - to winning the ultimate club prize in southern hemisphere rugby in the summer. Podcast: The remarkable rise of Clark Laidlaw 'Fully loaded' All Blacks out to preserve Scotland record Scotland lose Ritchie and Millar Mills through injury Eight of Laidlaw's Hurricanes players are in Dave Rennie's touring squad and it might have been double figures had injury not taken a number of others out of the reckoning. Laidlaw is a New Zealand passport holder now, but he'll be on Scotland's side on Saturday. "You're gonna see New Zealand's strongest possible team, but there's no reason why Scotland can't win," he reckons. "It's been a bounce of the ball here and there [in recent games]. "Scotland are definitely knocking on the door. I want Scotland to beat the All Blacks and I want the All Blacks to win every other game." He was 30 when he left Scotland for Taranaki, as a skills coach on the north island. Given his upbringing he always had a curiosity in him. His father always spoke about being a student of the game. "I just thought there must be different ways to look at the game and different ways to look at life, really," he explains. "I used to go and pass my rugby ball against a tree at lunchtime and train at night. I used to say to the old boys, I wasn't going to be staying here. "They'd be like, 'Yeah, you'll be here'. I just knew I didn't want to be there for 20 years. It's not like I had a bad life in Scotland. "I had a great job at East Lothian Council and I was coaching Jed-

item.title: Panthers Must Fix Left Tackle And Center Now
item.description: Bob Donnan-Imagn Images The Carolina Panthers offensive line is a mess, and the team cannot keep pretending it will fix itself. After a 27-19 loss to the Green Bay Packers on Thursday, the unit has become the main reason the offense stalls. Head coach Dave Canales acknowledged the possibility of changes in the offensive trenches. Swap the Starters at Center and Left Tackle First, the Panthers must bench veteran Luke Fortner at center. He has been a major disappointment for the team this year. Pro Football Focus reports Fortner has an overall grade of 53.3, placing him 30th among 35 qualifying centers. That is not good enough for a player who should be leading the line. Rookie Matt Hecht might not be perfect, but he cannot be worse than the current production. Hecht allowed just seven pressures in his final college season and zero sacks over 850 pass-blocking opportunities. The team should give the rookie a real shot to see if he can handle the job better than Fortner. Rasheed Walker was a bargain signing, but he has turned into the worst starter on the entire line. He keeps getting beat in pass protection and commits too many penalties. His PFF grade sits at 56.8, ranking 61st out of 71 qualifying offensive tackles across the league. Xavier Freeling, the replacement for 2026 first-round pick Ikem Ekwonu, is on the roster. Freeling spent practically his entire college career on the blindside at Georgia. For the remainder of the season, Freeling is slated to start at left tackle and Walker will move to the bench, per reports. This move alone could stop the constant pressure on the quarterback. Find a Real Tackle Before the Deadline Shuffling the bench players creates a hole on the right side. The logical name to fill that spot is Stone Forsythe, but he is not a great option. He is at best a below-average backup and cannot be counted on to start. With the NFL trade deadline approaching in one week, the Panthers must utilize it. They should look at Houston’s Braden Smith or Miami’s Austin Jackson. These players are available and would be a massive upgrade over what the team has now. The Panthers do not need to aim too high given their situation, but they must find someone who can actually protect the blindside. Canales said the changes come from the staff and their expectations for the players. “The urgency really just comes from myself, our staff, our expectations for our players, across the board,” Canales explained. The team is 3-4 and still leads the NFC South, but the record is misleading. The defense is struggling with injuries, and the offense cannot help them if the line keeps collapsing. Canales added that he wants his staff to feel confident in him. “We have a staff that’s committed to doing things the right way, and I want them to feel that confidence in me,” Canales added. The Panthers face the Denver Broncos on Sunday, Nov. 8 at Bank of America Stadium. The Broncos are a tough 6-2 team, and the Panthers need a solid offensive line to hav

item.title: Lionel Messi tops MLS jersey sales for fourth straight year as Robert Lewandowski surges and Cavan Sullivan cracks top 10
item.description: Atlanta United FC v Inter Miami CF - Getty Images Sport Messi leads the way again Messi's cultural impact on MLS and global football at large was once again clear in his jersey sales. Even if the eight-time Ballon d'Or winner saw his hold on the top spot in sales among all clubs worldwide snatched by Barcelona's Lamine Yamal, he remains the top dog in MLS for the fourth year in a row. His influence, no doubt, has Miami among the global leaders in merch sales. According to Marca , only four more clubs in football sold more kits than Miami - and no other MLS club cracked the top 10. Lewandowski gets World Cup bump Surprisingly, though, the World Cup saw a boost for foreign imports. Since his arrival in Chicago in June, Lewandowski led all players in jersey sales - including Messi. Antoine Griezmann, who signed for Orlando City in March but didn't feature until the summer, also cracked the top five after the World Cup. Cavan Sullivan creeping up the standings Cavan Sullivan creeping up the standings American influence in the top 10 was admittedly limited, with just one USMNT-er cracking the list. That player was Cavan Sullivan, who grabbed headlines by breaking several records for the Philadelphia Union after establishing himself as a first-team regular in June. His late-season surge, which saw him set a new record for goal contributions among MLS teenagers , pushed the previously down-and-out Union into a playoff spot. item.title: Arsenal star wants to leave in January with European giants interested
item.description: Arsenal star wants to leave in January with European giants interested Martin Zubimendi Ready for Arsenal Exit as January Transfer Interest Builds Across Europe Martin Zubimendi appears to be moving towards an early Arsenal departure, with the midfielder now prepared to explore a January transfer after a difficult spell in north London. According to TeamTalk , the 27-year-old has reached an “exit decision” and several major clubs across Europe have been made aware of his situation. Zubimendi joined Arsenal in a £60million deal in 2025 amid strong competition and significant expectation. He arrived as a player expected to anchor Mikel Arteta’s midfield for years to come. Instead, his role has diminished sharply, and the latest information suggests the Spain international now sees a move as the best route to revive his career. January transfer picture becoming clearer The report states that “Martin Zubimendi is ready to leave Arsenal in January in a bid to get his career back on track” and that “seven of the continent’s biggest clubs” have now been informed. There is strong interest from Spain, where Real Madrid, Barcelona and Atletico Madrid are all said to be attentive to the opportunity. Germany is also a live market. Bayern Munich and Borussia Dortmund have reportedly been made aware of his availability, while there has been contact in England too. Chelsea have been spoken to, and Liverpool have also been informed, although their current thinking is described as less advanced. That point matters. Liverpool’s earlier admiration belonged to a different period and a different structure, and there is no suggestion at present that they are pushing aggressively to bring him in. The broader theme here is that Arsenal are facing a serious possibility of movement, and rival clubs know it. Photo IMAGO Zubimendi Arsenal struggle leaves club with decision The most striking detail in the report is how far Zubimendi’s standing has fallen. He was signed to be a first-choice option, yet he is “yet to start a Premier League game this season”. For a player of his pedigree, and for a fee of £60million, that is a major development. Competition in midfield has intensified. The arrival of Bruno Guimaraes has altered the landscape further, while “the decision to promote Myles Lewis-Skelly ahead of him last season” underlined the shift long before this campaign gathered pace. Arsenal are understood to be aware of the player’s feelings and the possibility that he will seek a move once the window reopens. There is also acknowledgement that any deal will need careful handling. A loan has been mentioned as one possible route, though the financial structure would need to make sense for all parties. Arsenal are not dealing with a fringe academy product here, they are trying to manage the future of a recent £60million signing whose value and reputation still carry weight across Europe. item.title: Dean Wade’s $38M Sixers Deal Echoes The Controversial PJ Tucker Era
item.description: Bill Streicher-Imagn Images The Philadelphia 76ers paid Dean Wade $38.7 million for a role that looks a lot like the one P.J. Tucker played here. The front office signed Wade to a four-year deal, yet his early minutes show zero points in a recent game against the New York Knicks. This lack of scoring aggression feels familiar to fans who watched Tucker struggle to find the net during his only full season in Philadelphia. Wade has played just five games so far, averaging 3.6 points and 3.0 rebounds while attempting only 2.0 shots from deep per game. According to The Sixer Sense , his tenure with the team reflects the same situation the Sixers faced with PJ Tucker, who shot 1.9 threes per game and scored 3.5 points. The numbers are strikingly similar for two players brought in to space the floor and defend the perimeter. Zero Shots in 27 Minutes The silence on offense is the loudest part of this story. In the game versus the Knicks, Wade found numerous open opportunities but went without a single field goal attempt over 27 minutes. Against the Pistons, he took just five shots in 30 minutes, a meager output for someone holding a max-level contract. Although he notched 10 assists against the Pistons, surpassing his prior career high, the roster requires more than passing when the clock runs low. LeBron James has praised Wade’s impact, stating last week that “Dean is a perfect player for every team, and he’s going to make winning plays.” Tyrese Maxey echoed this sentiment, telling reporters, “It felt like he was everywhere, right?” when discussing Wade’s defensive presence. The praise is real, but the contract requires more than just good defense and high basketball IQ. A Historic Shooting Slump The stats from Yahoo Sports paint a grim picture for a shooter. Wade shoots 30 percent from three on minimal volume, while his average stands at 4.5 field goal attempts per 100 possessions. This mark stands as the lowest among all qualified players in the league. The Sixers urged him to increase his shooting during training camp, but the results have not followed the instruction. He is currently tallying 3.0 rebounds and 3.6 points per game, playing close to 28 minutes each night. The front office pursued him for his defensive versatility and connective passing, which he has shown. Yet, a $38 million player producing two scoreless games in his first five contests is difficult to justify for a championship contender. The Sixers need Wade to find his shot soon, or this contract will look like a mistake before the season even hits its midpoint.

item.title: Vic Fangio on Jonathan Greenard: ‘Practice is important. He’s had next to none.’
item.description: Photo by Mitchell Leff/Getty Images | Getty Images The Eagles defense has been inconsistent throughout the season, something defensive coordinator Vic Fangio highlighted when he spoke to reporters on Tuesday. He talked about self-scouting, what he saw from different players, and why Jonathan Greenard’s lack of practice has been so impactful. The DC also provided a short recap for their Sunday night loss to the Commanders. “Tough loss. We have to find a way to win those low-scoring games. We’ve done it here in the past. We’ve gotta be able to do it.” Here’s what else the DC had to say: On Jonathan Greenard “What I see, is a guy that’s had very, very little practice. I mean, when I say very little, miniscule. He missed all of training camp, missed the first two weeks of the season — no practice. Started practicing, was on a pitch count, played 19 plays, was gonna increase the next week, he got hurt early in that game. Didn’t finish that game. Didn’t play the next game. And, he’s been limited in practice. Contrary to some people’s popular belief, practice is important. He’s had next to none.” The only way to overcome that is with practice, explained Fangio. He noted that there was no magic pill or portion to catch up, no amount of watching tape or walkthroughs will make up for practice reps. Even for a veteran like Greenard, the DC was clear that practice matter. “Practice is important for everybody.” He went on to talk about Greenard is still finding his groove, and those practice reps are what will allow him to feel more comfortable in the system. It’s not for a lack of want to, or lack of effort, it’s just something that takes time executing what they’re asking of him and then carrying that over into games. Fangio also said that the bye week won’t offer any kind of catch-up period, noting that most teams don’t practice during the bye week, but that time might help Greenard get healthier. On Jordan Davis “He’s been not quite as good as he had been in the past, these last couple weeks. Think he’s got a little problem with his hand there, but he can be better. But we love Jordan [Davis] and he can get there.” On their self-scouting process Fangio said that they’re constantly evaluating things, and that it wouldn’t make sense to wait for the bye week to self-scout. It’s something they do every week. As for how he feels about their run defense to this point in the season, the DC said it’s been inconsistent. He thought it was okay, borderline good, but then at the end of the game gave up that 33-yarder. Fangio said that he needs to do a better job of coaching it and calling it, and then the players need to execute. On the Giants’ offense “They’ve got a really good offense They’ve got skill at the receiving position. They did a nice job raiding the Ravens, not just for John [Harbuagh], but with [Isaiah] Likely and [Patrick] Ricard. They got a lot of the Ravens-type offense that they had when Greg [Roman], and they’ve intermixed Kansas City-type passing

item.title: Oscar Goodman makes first start in Michigan's opener: 'Means a lot'
item.description: ANN ARBOR — Michigan coach Mike Boynton Jr. had several options and different ways he could’ve gone. With big man Moustapha Thiam missing the season opener against Oakland with an illness, Boynton could’ve inserted freshman Quinn Costello or veteran Jalen Reed at the power forward spot. He could’ve gone smaller and went with Ricky Liburd in the starting lineup. Instead, Boynton opted to give Oscar Goodman the nod and the first start of his college career. “I just thought Oscar has earned an opportunity,” Boynton said after Michigan’s 84-68 win at Crisler Center on Monday, Nov. 2. It’s one Goodman has been waiting for and working toward after joining the program midseason two years ago. The New Zealand native spent his first year on the scout team. Last season, he saw limited playing time primarily at the end of games while playing behind a loaded frontcourt that featured three lottery picks. On Monday, Goodman played meaningful minutes for the first time and had some good moments. In the first half, he grabbed a defensive rebound and threw a long outlet pass to J.P. Estrella for a fast-break layup. In the second half, he had a Euro-step finish in transition during a 9-0 run that put the game out of reach. He finished with six points, five rebounds, two assists, two steals and a blocked shot. He logged a career-high 22 minutes — double his previous high of 11 minutes last season. And while he shot 0-for-5 from 3-point range on a night the Wolverines were cold from deep, he didn’t stop letting it fly whenever he got a clean look. “I thought he played well enough,” Boynton said. “He was one of those guys that (had a) bunch of open shots, took good shots. What I'm glad is it didn't discourage him from rebounding and flying around on the defensive end because he still made a real positive impact on the game.” That showed in the plus-minus rating, where Goodman was a plus-23 against the Golden Grizzlies. That was the second-best mark on the team behind Estrella’s plus-25 rating. “I think I did pretty well,” said Goodman, who dealt with a tweaked back in the preseason. “I came out with some rebounds when we needed them and just kept shooting the ball. I need to keep shooting it, just stay confident in myself and they're going to drop eventually.” A little Euro step from the New Zealander‼️ 📺: @BigTenNetwork pic.twitter.com/S6Oda6aOhF — Michigan Men's Basketball (@umichbball) November 3, 2026 According to Goodman, Boynton informed him during Sunday’s practice that Thiam was going to be out and he was going to start. For someone who had to wait his turn and sacrificed playing time that he could’ve received elsewhere, getting that opportunity “means a lot.” “It was awesome. I called my parents. My brother is in town, so that was cool for him to see that,” Goodman said. “I was really excited, really happy for the moment, knowing the past year was put to good use. “I've never really not played before in my career. I think that little bump in the journey help

item.title: Simms Says Cowboys Growing Impatient With Dak Prescott Amid $131 Million Risk
item.description: Bill Streicher-Imagn Images Former NFL quarterback Chris Simms believes the Dallas Cowboys are running out of patience with Dak Prescott. After a tough loss to the Arizona Cardinals on Sunday, Simms told listeners on his podcast that the team might be ready to move on. He noted that the franchise could be “at the end of their rope” with the veteran player if things do not improve quickly. The pressure is real, but the price to leave is even higher. Dallas signed Prescott to a massive four-year, $240 million extension in September 2024. That deal keeps him under contract through the 2028 season and includes $231 million in total guarantees. The team faces a nightmare scenario if they try to cut him now, as reported by Yahoo Sports . The Cost of Moving On Money is the main reason the Cowboys might keep Prescott despite the chatter. Dallas would face approximately $131 million in dead money if the player is cut prior to June 1, per reports. Even waiting until after June 1 does not solve the problem, as the team would still owe about $76 million. A trade offers slightly better relief but still carries a heavy cost of $86 million before the June deadline. These numbers mean the front office cannot just wave a wand and start over. The void years on Prescott’s deal, which run from 2029 through 2032, push the financial pain into the future. Sports Illustrated reported that the dead money hits would linger through 2030 because of these specific contract terms. Jerry Jones knows that paying for a player who does not start is bad business, but paying double for a new one is worse. Performance Under the Microscope Simms argues that Prescott simply does not match up with the best in the league. He stated on “PFT Live” that “Dak is not one of the top quarterbacks in football. That’s not even debatable.” While Prescott ranks first in the NFL in first downs and fifth in passing yards, his contract tells a different story. His deal averages $60 million per season, which ranks second in the entire league behind Patrick Mahomes. The Cowboys fell to a 3-5 record after their overtime loss to Arizona. This drop comes after Prescott led the team to only a 2-5 record in the postseason. On the Chris Simms Unbuttoned podcast, Chris Simms observed that “Like, it’s like things better turn around or he ain’t gonna be the quarterback there next year.” The window to prove he belongs at that price is closing fast. A Look at the Future If the Cowboys do decide to make a change, they have a specific target in mind. Simms suggested on “PFT Live” that “They’re going to want Mike Tomlin” as an eventual replacement for the current coaching staff. This points to a desire for a leader who can fix the culture on the field. The team needs a new identity if they want to win big again. Among NFL quarterbacks this season, Prescott holds the 12th rank with a 79.6 PFN Impact Score. That number sits in the middle of the pack for a player earning the second-highest salary. item.title: Nigeria needs 10% growth to reduce poverty — Peterside
item.description: By Favour Ulebor, Abuja Businessman and former Nigerian Stock Exchange chairman, Atedo Peterside, has said Nigeria’s economic growth rate of about four per cent is inadequate to generate the jobs and investment needed to lift citizens out of poverty, insisting that the country must target annual growth of 10 per cent. Peterside spoke on Tuesday at the second Oxford Global Think Tank Leadership Conference in Abuja, where he identified declining investment, corruption, political patronage and the misuse of public resources as major obstacles to stronger economic growth. He said Nigeria’s investment-to-Gross Domestic Product (GDP) ratio had declined steadily since 1999, despite the optimism that followed the return to democratic rule, when local and foreign investors showed renewed interest in the economy. According to him, investors have been discouraged by an environment where access to opportunities is often determined by political connections, while small and medium-sized enterprises face harassment from regulatory authorities. Peterside called for an economy in which investors could operate without relying on political connections, stressing that public resources must be channelled into productive ventures to achieve the country’s growth ambitions. He warned against celebrating modest economic growth while corruption and the diversion of public funds persisted, arguing that procurement processes could be manipulated to enrich individuals at the expense of development. “Procurement can become legalised theft,” he said, citing inflated contracts and the award of projects to politically connected business partners as practices that undermine the effective use of public funds. Peterside maintained that Nigeria could not move from four per cent to 10 per cent growth without tackling corruption and ensuring that government resources were invested productively. Also speaking, the Emir of Kano, Muhammadu Sanusi II, acknowledged improvements in some economic indicators but cautioned that headline growth figures did not necessarily reflect the welfare of Nigerians. Sanusi said the country’s economic growth of about 4.5 per cent represented progress compared with previous years, but argued that economic performance should be measured by its impact on people’s lives, rather than GDP figures alone. The former Governor of the Central Bank of Nigeria said the depreciation of the naira had affected GDP per capita, making it necessary to consider the relationship between economic growth, currency movements and household purchasing power. He said the economy should also be assessed through access to education, healthcare, nutrition and employment, as well as the distribution of economic opportunities across the country. Sanusi questioned the significance of headline economic figures if poverty, unemployment and hardship remained widespread. item.title: Rutgers Athletics Launches ‘Rutgers Tough’ Campaign to Support Cancer Treatment
item.description: Rutgers Athletics is bringing the Scarlet Knights community together for a cause that extends well beyond the basketball court. The university announced the launch of its Rutgers Tough fundraising campaign, an initiative designed to support RWJBarnabas Health’s cancer treatment and patient-care efforts. The campaign was inspired by men’s basketball head coach Steve Pikiell and his wife, Kate, following Pikiell’s cancer diagnosis in September. The initiative will allow Rutgers fans to support cancer treatment and patient care through limited-edition merchandise and additional donations to cancer research. The campaign’s central component is a limited-edition Rutgers Tough T-shirt, which will be available for $30 at the first three men’s basketball home games of the season. Those games include the November 6 matchup against New Haven, November 10 against NJIT, and November 13 against Bryant. All proceeds from the t-shirt sales will benefit RWJBarnabas Health. Fans can also contribute directly to cancer research through a fund supporting the Rutgers Cancer Institute. The campaign comes after Pikiell publicly announced his diagnosis on September 9. Following surgery, the longtime Rutgers head coach expressed gratitude for the medical teams supporting him and his family as he continues treatment. Pikiell has also spoken about how his experience has changed his perspective on the people around him, particularly Rutgers fans who are dealing with cancer themselves. During an appearance on his podcast in October, Pikiell discussed receiving messages from season-ticket holders going through similar experiences. He reflected on how attending games and following their teams can provide people with something positive to look forward to during difficult periods in their lives. He also emphasized the importance of helping patients who may not have access to the healthcare and medication they need. “Rutgers has an unbelievable cancer institute, and RWJBarnabas, so many good things, I said we got to raise money, we got to help any way that we can, my wife and I have donated personally, you know, a large sum of money that I hope goes towards research, and I hope it goes towards helping people, and now I want to raise money for people that don’t have healthcare, and need cancer medicine, and need those things, and Rutgers has jumped on board and campaigned as Rutgers toughness, because I always said, you got to have a little more toughness at Rutgers,” Pikiell stated on his podcast. Both Pikiell and his wife have personally contributed to cancer research and now hope to use Rutgers’ platform to encourage others to get involved. The campaign has also received support from several former Scarlet Knights basketball players. item.title: Georgia football coach Kirby Smart previews Ole Miss game
item.description: Georgia Bulldogs head coach Kirby Smart heavily praised Ole Miss Rebels quarterback Trinidad Chambliss during his weekly press conference. Smart is quite familiar with Chambliss and Ole Miss . Georgia played Chambliss twice last year including in the Sugar Bowl, which the Rebels won 39-34. Georgia won the regular season meeting in Athens, 43-35. Georgia (7-1, 5-1 SEC) and Ole Miss (6-2, 4-2 SEC) are both in the thick of the SEC championship and College Football Playoff hunt. The winner on Saturday night (7:30 p.m. ET on Nov. 7) will find themselves in a much better position while the losers will find themselves much worse off. Specifically, Ole Miss could be facing playoff elimination with a loss to Georgia since the Rebels have an ugly blowout loss to Florida. We're likely looking at another high-stakes shootout between Georgia and Ole Miss. Here's what Georgia coach Kirby Smart said about Ole Miss with most of the media's questions focusing on Chambliss. Smart's opening statement on Ole Miss "It's on to Ole Miss, a really good football team," Smart said at his weekly press conference. "Pete (Golding) has done a tremendous job since taking over. "Obviously, we know the two games last year with them were both really hard-fought battles, hard games, a lot of ebb-and-flow in both games. They've done a tremendous job this year. They probably have the best quarterback in the country who plays at a high level. He is extremely hard to defend and a great player. "I have a lot of respect for their staff. I know a lot of those guys and the team, the way their team competes and plays. They're playing really well right now. At home, they've been exceptionally well. Our guys will be excited for the challenge. Another opportunity. Another week in the SEC, as it always is. It'll be a great atmosphere." On how to defend Chambliss "How long do you have?" Smart said. "We could talk for an hour about it, but it's not even that. "I wrote down, so I watched every game, wow plays. It's not the wow plays. The wow plays are what you guys love and what America loves. He had some wow plays against us last year in both games, but especially the second. "It's the down-in, down-out decision making that he's really elite at. The accuracy that he's elite at, the release, the decision. His pinpointing. He has an anticipation of windows that's probably unmatched. I don't know if that was God-given or the fact that he played a lot of football before he got to Ole Miss. He has played a lot of football and experience helps. "You throw all that in, and you have a tremendous athlete. He goes forwards, backwards as fast as he goes sideways. He can back up and go for it. He's just a great athlete that is a great quarterback." On Chambliss' pre-snap and post-snap ability "I can't get inside his head and say what he's doing pre-snap, post-snap," Smart adds. "He's elite at both, in my opinion. He surveys the field. He knows what he's going to do. He's been in this offense long enough tha

item.title: LeBron’s Wine Sip Proves The 76ers Are Finally Having Fun
item.description: Bill Streicher-Imagn Images During Monday night’s contest versus the Chicago Bulls, LeBron James sampled some red wine belonging to a fan. The Philadelphia 76ers won that matchup 126 to 107. James finished with 15 points, 7 rebounds, and 9 assists while the team moved to a 7-1 record on the season. The star player is no longer just grinding through the long season; he is enjoying the ride again. The moment happened in the third quarter when James chased a loose ball and crashed into fan Troy Clemons. Clemons was holding a cup of red wine, which is James’ favorite drink. James spilled some of the wine on himself and decided to taste it right there on the floor. He later told reporters, “I wanted to see if it was worth it on my arm, how good it was. It was all right,” per ESPN . This wasn’t a planned stunt or a media event. It was a spontaneous reaction to a messy play. Sports often feel like a serious job for players, but this incident shows James treating the game like a party. He danced after an and-one layup that made guard Tyrese Maxey laugh. He also danced with Maxey later when the point guard scored his own and-one basket. These are the small moments that keep a player fresh. James explained the need for this joy clearly. He said, “Listen, it’s a long marathon. If you don’t find ways to have fun throughout it, even though you’re working, even though you’re locked in, then it could wear on you,” according to ESPN. Clemons, the fan who lost his wine, did not mind the exchange at all. He told ESPN, “I’m just glad for him to be here.” He even added, “I’m not worried about the wine getting on me.” The fan threw the cup away and got a fresh drink. He now has a story that will last a lifetime. The 76ers are 7-1, and the atmosphere in the arena feels lighter. This is what a winning team looks like when the players are actually happy. A Pattern of Fun in Philadelphia James has a history of playful moments involving alcohol during games. After missing a shot in 2017, he seized a beer bottle from a vendor, feigned drinking from it, then returned the bottle. That was a different time, but the spirit remains the same. On Monday, the interaction was more direct and personal. ESPN’s Kris Rhim posted a video of the event on X, captioning it, “Here’s vid of LeBron taking a sip of a drink from a fan just now during tonight’s game.” The video went viral because it felt real and unscripted. The 76ers face the Detroit Pistons on Wednesday. The Pistons are the only team to beat Philadelphia this season. The team needs to keep this fun energy if they want to stay on top. James noted that the fans are great to them, so they try to be great to the fans by playing hard and being showmen. The wine sip was just one part of a great game for the Sixers. The numbers show they are winning, but the smile on James’ face shows they are enjoying it. The final score was 126-107, and the team took a wine sip. item.title: Patrick Kane Injury Sides Blackhawks, Missing Next Games
item.description: David Banks-Imagn Images The return of a legend hit a sudden snag on Monday night. Patrick Kane left the ice during the second period against Colorado and never came back. The Chicago Blackhawks confirmed he will sit out the next couple of games due to an upper-body injury. This loss comes right after a 5-2 defeat to the Avalanche, a result that already stung the home crowd. Head coach Jeff Blashill spoke clearly about the situation after the game. According to his statement, an upper-body injury has sidelined Kane for a minimum of two upcoming matches. The exact cause of the hurt remains unclear to the public. Before retreating to the locker room, Kane appeared to struggle physically, suggesting an underlying issue. His absence creates a gap in the lineup. A Heavy Loss for the Lineup The numbers show just how vital Kane is to this squad right now. At 37 years old, he has recorded one goal and eight assists for nine points in 14 games this season. Daily Faceoff reports he now shares the team’s top scoring spot with center Connor Bedard. The team will be without the player who shares the top spot with the franchise’s young star, a playmaker who creates scoring chances. Blashill noted the team must adjust without their veteran leader. The exact timeline for his return depends on how his body heals over the next few days. Fans saw him struggle near the end of the second period before the medical staff stepped in. The team released a brief statement confirming he will not return to the game on Monday, Nov. 2. This uncertainty hangs over the locker room as they prepare for their next opponent. History on the Line Kane’s journey back to Chicago was meant to be a celebration of his past glory. He signed a two-year, $16 million contract as an unrestricted free agent this past offseason. Prior to this, he played the preceding three seasons alongside the Detroit Red Wings. His legacy in Chicago is untouchable, having played his first 15-plus NHL seasons there. He won three Stanley Cups and earned the Conn Smythe Trophy as playoff MVP in 2013. His Hart Trophy win in 2016 proved he was the best player in the league during the regular season. He now sits second only to Stan Mikita on the Blackhawks’ historical scoring chart. Being named one of the NHL’s 100 Greatest Players in 2017 shows his standing in the sport. In 67 contests during the previous season, Kane recorded 16 goals and 41 assists totaling 57 points. Those stats prove he can still produce at a high level despite his age. Now, the team faces a test without its most experienced scorer. RotoWire reports that Ben Pope of the Chicago Sun-Times confirmed the injury details as well.

item.title: Morgan Scalley admits he was ‘dead wrong’ about Bear Bachmeier ahead of Utah-BYU Holy War game
item.description: Morgan Scalley will coach his first Holy War as head of the Utah Utes at noon ET on Saturday, when the No. 4 Utes bring an 8-0 record into Rice-Eccles Stadium against the No. 8 BYU Cougars. At his Monday news conference, the talk turned to BYU quarterback Bear Bachmeier, and Scalley opened with an admission about his own first impression. “I’m going to be honest. When I first started watching Bear, I’m like, ‘This guy cannot throw. He’s a running back playing quarterback.’ I was wrong, dead wrong. I mean, Aaron Roderick has done such a great job developing him and you can tell his work ethic also. You have to compliment him on that because he is an efficient thrower. He has zip on his ball. He makes great decisions. Add to that, the fact that when he runs, it’s like, OK, bring your lunch every time. He is thick, he’s tough to bring down, really good balance. So the dual threat is always going to be something that if team’s got that, then you really have to have answers and take your shots every once in a while, but can’t say enough good things about him,” Scalley said. Scalley’s answer fits what he laid out at Big 12 media days in July, when he talked about the example he and BYU coach Kalani Sitake want to set for both fan bases. “I just think the way Kalani and I model our relationship with one another, the respect we have for each other and our programs should lead the way,” Scalley said . Praising a rival quarterback by name during Holy War week is a small thing, and it still marks a clear change in how the head coach at Utah handles this game. item.title: Mike Brown Says Knicks Chemistry Starts From Base Camp
item.description: Brad Penner-Imagn Images Last season’s momentum has not been maintained by the New York Knicks as they move forward. Mike Brown, the head coach, stated the squad must restart from base camp to forge championship chemistry. The defending champions have stumbled to a 3-4 record through the first seven games of the 2026-27 campaign. Brown informed reporters that chemistry cannot be stored in a locker for future use. He compared the current season to a grueling mountain hike where skipping steps leads to disaster, according to Yahoo Sports . The core group of players knows each other well, yet the offense still looks disjointed and slow to find its rhythm. The coach stressed that the group must proceed correctly at every step while rebuilding their identity. Mikal Bridges agreed, noting the team requires time to regain sync following the June break. The gap between the end of last season and now has cost the team its flow and sharpness. Bridges observed that the performance decline mirrors the adjustment period needed for the new year. Brown feels the squad must create high-quality three-point looks to clear the paint for big men. Missing those shots requires better movement and play elsewhere to prevent defensive traps. Bridges Struggles in a Deep Slump Mikal Bridges has faced significant challenges in his scoring ability during the early part of the season. Over seven games, Bridges averages 6.1 points, 2.7 rebounds, and 1.7 assists on 30.8 percent shooting. These numbers represent a steep drop from last season when he averaged 14.4 points and shot 49 percent from the floor. Bridges has reached double figures in scoring just twice in seven appearances this year, with a season-high of 12 points against both Detroit and Philadelphia. Brown remains calm regarding a key contributor to last season’s Knicks title push who is struggling. He insists that Bridges must find a way to stay productive even when his shots are not falling. The coach has reduced Bridges’ playing time in recent games as he tries to ride the hot hands of other players. In the win over the Brooklyn Nets on Monday, Bridges played just 16 minutes and scored only six points on 1-of-7 shooting. He went scoreless on two three-point attempts, ending with two rebounds and zero assists. Brown noted that strong reserve play led to Bridges spending significant time on the bench. Landry Shamet scored a game-high 22 points off the bench, and Jordan Clarkson added seven points in 11 minutes to help New York outscore Brooklyn in the fourth quarter. The coach thinks Bridges can exit the slump by focusing on game aspects independent of shooting. He told reporters that during a funk, one must find one or two things to hold their hat on. Mikal ranks among the NBA’s best runners in both offensive and defensive directions. Therefore, he must lean on that running, along with cutting, rebounding, and driving. item.title: Eduardo Camavinga talks Vinicius, Mourinho, Bernardo Silva, Real Madrid future and personal transformation ahead of AEK Athens clash
item.description: Eduardo Camavinga talks Vinicius, Mourinho, Bernardo Silva, Real Madrid future and personal transformation ahead of AEK Athens clash Real Madrid are looking to continue their winning run when they face AEK Athens in the UEFA Champions League on Wednesday. Los Blancos come into this game with six consecutive wins, and Jose Mourinho will want his team to keep up the momentum in Greece. Ahead of the encounter, Eduardo Camavinga spoke openly about his difficult summer, his relationship with Jose Mourinho and the changes he made to his preparations. On his difficult summer and personal transformation The French midfielder began his press conference by expressing his condolences following the tragic death of Tenerife footballer Jesus de Miguel. “First, before we begin, I would like to express my condolences to the family of Jesus de Miguel,” he said. Reflecting on the uncertainty surrounding his future, Camavinga admitted: “To be honest, it was a tough, difficult time for me.” Eduardo Camavinga is likely to start alongside Bernardo Silva for Real Madrid tomorrow. (Photo by Angel Martinez/Getty Images) “I’ve worked very hard this summer, and I’m a new man. I have more discipline than before. I’m working to repay the trust the club has placed in me,” he explained. Explaining his transformation, he added: “I went back to school, it was a very different experience.” “I worked on things I don’t usually do, discipline, for instance, arriving two or three hours early to work in the gym. My mindset has also changed. I’m a bit more mature.” Camavinga on Mourinho, Vinicius and Bernardo Silva Camavinga also praised Mourinho’s influence on his development and spoke about his relationship with the manager. “He’s a very likeable person, he’s a great coach with a rich history. You learn a lot from him every day, about the mindset you need to have on the pitch,” the Frenchman said. The 23-year-old was then quizzed on whether he could have imagined Vinicius Jr. leaving the club back in the summer. “Actually, no, I wouldn’t, because Vini has been a Madridista since he was a child. He loves the club. I would never imagine that he would want to leave,” he said. On Bernardo Silva, he said: “He’s a great player. He helps us a lot in possession and build-up.” Camavinga speaks about dressing-room unity Camavinga dismissed suggestions that Real Madrid’s earlier struggles were due to a lack of unity in the dressing room. “We have always had a good relationship, we have always been a united team. But when the results aren’t good, you assume there’s something wrong in the dressing room,” he said. Camavinga’s fortunes are slowly improving at Real Madrid. (Photo by Denis Doyle/Getty Images) Finally, the French midfield star spoke about Real Madrid’s ambitions. “Our job is to win every match. We’ve started the season well, and we need to keep it up,” he concluded. Camavinga’s appearance before the media ahead of the game suggests he is likely to start against AEK Athens tomorrow. Au

item.title: What will 'exciting' McNamara bring to Leinster?
item.description: After much speculation, Noel McNamara has been handed the keys at Leinster to replace outgoing head coach Leo Cullen. McNamara is currently attacking coach at Bordeaux Begles, and helped to mastermind a dominating victory over Leinster in the Investec Champions Cup final in May. When he was announced, McNamara described the Leinster job as "one of the most prestigious roles in world rugby". But what will the 43-year-old bring to the Irish province when he takes over next year? Ireland full-back Hugo Keenen has a long-standing relationship with McNamara, which goes back to when he was playing for UCD in the All-Ireland League, and he said it was "great news". McNamara to succeed Cullen as Leinster head coach The pair would have more interactions at Leinster when McNamara was working at the province as academy manager and Leinster A's head coach. After five years in Dublin, where he also coached Ireland's Under-20s to Grand Slam success in 2019, McNamara made the move to South Africa in 2021 to join the Sharks as attack and backs coach. From there, he joined Bordeaux in 2023 and has helped the French side to back-to-back European titles. Keenan, who is in Ireland camp ahead of November's Nations Championship matches, said it was "an exciting appointment". "It's good to have him on board and I think that's the general feedback amongst the squad," Keenan said. "I'm sure he's got a different perspective of things, by getting out of the building, going down to South Africa, challenging himself down there, and going so well and thriving at Bordeaux." 'Presence in a room' Leinster know first hand what a McNamara-led attack can do, which was evident in the Champions Cup final in May. The Irish province had no answer to Bordeaux in Bilbao as the French outfit made it consecutive European crowns with a crushing 41-19 win. After that win, McNamara told BBC Sport he had used Rory McIlroy, who had not long won back-to-back at the Masters, as motivation for his players. McNamara had also spoken about Leinster's character in bouncing back after so many defeats, and said "tough times create tough people". "Obviously, we know what he's achieved at Bordeaux and he's been on the better side of a few results than us recently," Keenan added. "You see what their backline and attacks have been producing, and I suppose that's his fingerprint on it. "I'm excited to see what he has and to work with him. I think it's positive for me and everyone at Leinster." Keenan added that the departing Cullen was "big boots to fill" after a trophy-laden 12 years with Leinster. Noel McNamara will replace Leo Cullen (left) as Leinster head coach [Getty Images] The former Ireland second row has led Leinster to six league titles and the Champions Cup in 2018, but his side subsequently lost five finals in the competition, including four in the past five years.
