item.title: Zamfara APC primary: My mandate cannot be stolen — Kaura
item.description: By Idris Salisu, Gusau Senator Tijjani Yahaya Kaura, who contested the All Progressives Congress (APC) primary election for Zamfara North Senatorial District, has insisted that his mandate cannot be taken away from him. Kaura made the assertion while addressing a press conference at his residence in Kaura Namoda, where he claimed that he had been officially declared winner by members of the primary election committee sent by the APC national headquarters. He alleged that the committee’s chairman was taken to an undisclosed location by some individuals he described as anti-democratic elements. According to the senator, the chairman was abducted and subsequently announced a result declaring Senator Sahabi Ya’u winner, but a majority of the committee members rejected the announcement and jointly declared him winner. Kaura described the alleged abduction as an attempt to undermine democracy, insisting that the electorate would not accept such an outcome. He also dismissed the opposing camp’s claim that Sahabi had been declared winner, describing the announcement as invalid. The senator said APC members had turned out in large numbers to vote for him as the party’s candidate for Zamfara North in the 2027 general elections. He thanked the electorate for the confidence reposed in him and urged political stakeholders to respect what he described as the people’s mandate and the result announced by the committee members. The post Zamfara APC primary: My mandate cannot be stolen — Kaura appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Hawks Win Looks Good But Hides Real Problems Against Six Pacers
item.description: Trevor Ruszkowski-Imagn Images Atlanta needed a miracle just to beat a Pacers team that had no legs left. The Hawks escaped with a 108-104 win on Monday night in Indianapolis, but the final score tells a lie about how close this game actually was. Nickeil Alexander-Walker poured in 34 points and tied his career high with nine three-pointers, per Peachtree Hoops. Yet the team still let a squad with only six healthy players cut a 15-point lead down to two points in the final minutes. This was not a dominant performance. It was a lucky escape. A Salary Gap That Should Not Matter The story of this game was not the Hawks; it was the massive payroll the Pacers left on the bench. According to reports, the sidelined players totaled roughly $193 million in salary, whereas active court players earned approximately $15 million. Tyrese Haliburton, Pascal Siakam, and T.J. McConnell were all out, leaving Indiana with just six available bodies. Even with that huge gap, the Hawks struggled to put the game away. They shot just 28% from the field in the third quarter and endured a nearly four-minute field goal drought in the fourth. You do not get that kind of scare against a full-strength team. The Cost of a Bad Clutch Finish Atlanta had leads of 14 and 15 points but let them slip away due to poor execution down the stretch. Onyeka Okongwu finally hit a hook shot with 10.2 seconds left to secure a four-point lead, but the Pacers still had one more stop to make. Quenton Jackson missed a potential game-tying three-pointer with 43.1 seconds remaining, saving the Hawks from total embarrassment. The Pacers played with zero rest, as all six players logged between 34 and 45 minutes. Pacers coach Rick Carlisle admitted after the game that “These guys all played too many minutes,” according to theScore . If the Pacers had just one more body, the Hawks might have lost this one. Can This Team Handle Real Pressure? Head coach Quin Snyder called it a “really good win,” but the stats show a team that is still fragile when things get tight. The Hawks scored only 26 points in the paint all night, relying almost entirely on outside shooting to survive. Nickeil Alexander-Walker hit 15 of his 3-point attempts, and the team made 15 threes in the first half alone, tying a franchise record. But once the shooting cooled, the offense stalled completely. The Hawks will face the Washington Wizards on Wednesday, and they need to fix their interior scoring before that game. A win against a six-man team does not prove anything about their ability to beat a real contender.

item.title: Hornets’ 33-Point Loss Shows Detroit Is Now A Real Threat
item.description: Jim Dedmon-Imagn Images The Detroit Pistons didn’t just beat the Hornets; they crushed them by 33 points in a 124-91 rout. Cade Cunningham led the way with a season-high 33 points, adding seven assists and five steals to show why he is the engine of this new Pistons squad. Sports Illustrated reports that this commanding win cements their spot near the summit of early Eastern Conference rankings, representing their best season opener in more than ten years. The Turnover Problem Is Real The Hornets cannot keep turning the ball over like this. They coughed up 27 possessions to Detroit, which gave the Pistons easy points on the fast break. Yahoo Sports notes the Hornets stand alone as the sole NBA franchise averaging under 100 points per game, with a figure of 97.4. When you add in their 29.6% shooting from deep, the offense looks stuck. Brandon Miller tried to keep things close with 17 points, but it wasn’t enough to stop the bleeding. The Pistons forced 27 turnovers and used those stops to build a massive lead that the Hornets could never touch. Duncan Robinson Is the Difference Maker In his first start of the season, he made six of his nine 3-point attempts and scored 24 points. His energy sparked a 27-2 run in the third quarter that effectively ended the game. Robinson explained the shift simply after the game. “We got stops,” Duncan Robinson commented on that key moment. “I think they were stuck at 75 for a while. When we get stops, the game becomes really easy for us.” The Pistons also got 11 points from Ron Holland II, who stayed in the game late and kept the pressure on. This depth is what separates a good team from a great one. Charlotte fans are used to seeing their team struggle, but this loss feels different. The Hornets led the league in 3-pointers made last season, yet they are now tied for 16th in makes this year. Naz Reid is averaging a career-high 15.5 points, but his shooting percentage has dropped to 39.5%. The team needs to find a way to score without relying solely on the outside shot. Detroit has shown they can punish teams that make mistakes, and the Hornets made plenty of them. The Pistons will host the Philadelphia 76ers on Wednesday, but the Hornets face the Brooklyn Nets on the road.

item.title: Chiefs Rookie Delane Faces Long Road Back From Shoulder Injury
item.description: Joe Nicholson-Imagn Images The Kansas City Chiefs are watching their rookie cornerback, Mansoor Delane, closely as he tries to get his shoulder strong enough to play. Head coach Andy Reid gave fans a mixed update after the team lost to the Denver Broncos on Sunday. While Delane has played well this season, his right shoulder keeps acting up and might be a problem for the rest of the year. The team needs him back, but safety comes first. Reid said on Monday that the rookie could return for the game against the New York Jets, yet he warned that the injury is not going away quickly. Delane missed the last game against Denver even though he was listed as questionable before the start. The issue started back in the offseason during organized team activities and has troubled him ever since. He aggravated the shoulder during a Week 1 win over the Broncos and sat out the rest of that game plus all of Week 2. He played in four straight games after returning, but the pain flared up again in practice last Wednesday. This forced the Chiefs to rule him out for Sunday’s matchup at Empower Field at Mile High. A Day-By-Day Battle for Strength The coaching staff will not rush Delane back until his body is ready. Reid explained that the team will check on him every single day to see how he feels. “It’s just a matter of it being strong enough to get out there,” Reid said. The coach added that there is a chance Delane can play in Week 9, but it depends entirely on how strong the shoulder gets. “There’s a chance that he’ll be able to get himself out there this week. Again, it’s just how strong it is. It’s going to be a day-to-day thing,” Reid told reporters. The first practice of the week on Wednesday will show if he can take the field. Delane has shown he is a key player when healthy. Yahoo Sports reports that in five games this season, he has posted 27 tackles, five passes defended, and one interception. The team allowed 28 points to Denver, their second-highest total of the season, partly because they were without their rookie star in the secondary. Delane was absent, and the defense allowed Bo Nix and the Broncos offense to score. Depth Options and Roster Moves The Chiefs have other options to fill the corner spot while Delane heals. Veteran L’Jarius Sneed is already on injured reserve, which left the team thin in the backfield. Rookie Canady stepped up in Week 8 and made two tackles against Denver, including a big stop in the open field. Chris Roland-Wallace has also played well in the slot, posting 86 tackles and two interceptions over his three years with the team. To make room for these younger players, the Chiefs cut veteran Kader Kohou from their practice squad on Monday. Kohou had signed a one-year deal in the offseason but never cracked the main roster. “The Chiefs terminated the practice squad contract of CB Kader Kohou,” A to Z Sports’ Charles Goldman wrote on X. This move opens two spots on the practice squad and signals that the team is looking to dev

item.title: 76ers' Tyrese Maxey makes franchise history only Allen Iverson, Wilt Chamberlain have made
item.description: 76ers' Tyrese Maxey makes franchise history only Allen Iverson, Wilt Chamberlain have made originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . While LeBron James, Jaylen Brown and Joel Embiid get most of the attention for the Philadelphia 76ers , it is Tyrese Maxey who should really be putting fear into opposing teams. The guard out of Kentucky is one of the shiftiest players in the entire NBA. Maxey continues to get better with every game. Over the weekend, in a game where James and Embiid were both sidelined, he went nuclear. “Tyrese Maxey tonight as the 76ers improve to 6-1 this season: 38 points (15 in 4Q), 4 rebounds, 4 assists, 2 steals. This is the third time this season that he has scored 15+ points in the fourth quarter,” ClutchPoints wrote. On Monday, it was more of the same for Maxey, particularly in the fourth quarter, when he took over the game. It wasn't a particularly high-scoring night for the guard — at least until the fourth quarter. “Tyrese Maxey scored 15 of his 26 points in the fourth quarter and dished out 11 assists to highlight the Philadelphia 76ers' 126-107 victory over the visiting Chicago Bulls on Monday,” The News Tribune wrote. In the game against the Chicago Bulls, Maxey made franchise history, joining an exclusive group that includes some of the greatest players to ever wear a 76ers uniform. Maxey became just the third player in franchise history to accomplish the feat, joining Allen Iverson and Wilt Chamberlain. “Tyrese Maxey is the third player in 76ers history with 20+ games of 25 points and 10 assists, joining Allen Iverson (65) and Wilt Chamberlain (25),” ESPN’s Kris Rhim posted. This shows just how special Maxey is, especially with so many weapons around him to whom he can distribute the ball. While he has a knack for scoring, it is also clear that he can set his teammates up and get them involved. The guard out of Kentucky has been a special find for Philadelphia since he was drafted, and he continues to prove that. Now, playing alongside some of the best in the world, his game continues to evolve, with his latest accomplishment putting him in the history books alongside 76ers legends. item.title: Steelers DC Patrick Graham ranked one of the the NFL’s best new coordinators
item.description: Mandatory Credit: Barry Reeger-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Sunday, as Pittsburgh moved to 6-2 and gained sole possession of first place in the AFC North. The Steelers’ defense has come alive over the last month, thanks to their new defensive coordinator, Patrick Graham. CBS Sports ranked the NFL’s best new coordinators at midseason , and Graham earned the number two spot overall on the list. “The Pittsburgh Steelers’ defense has come back to life under new defensive coordinator Patrick Graham,” Garrett Podell writes. “They’re the league’s No. 3 scoring defense (18.0 points per game allowed), No. 6 total defense (305.6 total yards per game allowed), No. 3 run defense (83.9 rushing yards per game allowed), No. 8 third down defense (34.3% third down conversion rate allowed), No. 2 red zone defense (37.5% third down conversion rate allowed), and tied for No. 3 in takeaways (13).” “Having All-Pro edge rusher T.J. Watt turning back the clock also helps. After he had just 7.0 sacks in 14 games last season, Watt has 7.5 in eight games this season, which is tied for the league lead with Houston Texans All-Pro edge rusher Will Anderson Jr. No team has more sacks in the NFL than Graham’s unit’s 26, one more than the Brian Flores blitzkrieg Minnesota Vikings attack. ” “The Browns were flying high entering Week 8 with a 5-2 record, but they left Pittsburgh 5-3 after a 27-6 defeat in which the Steelers held them to both season-lows in points (6) and rushing yards (34). Graham is crushing it.” Graham was behind only Packers defensive coordinator Jonathan Gannon on the list. Graham joined the Steelers staff after spending the previous four seasons as the defensive coordinator of the Las Vegas Raiders. Graham’s zone-heavy defense has done wonders for the unit. Take this past weekend, for example, as the team recorded eight sacks against Cleveland. The Steelers can finally say they once again have an elite defense to help them in their playoff push as they enter the second half of their 2026 campaign. With Graham in charge and the abundance of talent on the unit, it seems like the Steelers are destined to have their first top-10 scoring defense since the 2023 season. Graham deserves all of the praise he is getting from the media. Let us know what you think in the comments . Be sure to bookmark Behind the Steel Curtain for all the latest news, breakdowns, and more! item.title: ‘So fake’… NBA fans react to LeBron James saying he enjoyed being Russell Westbrook’s teammate
item.description: Photo by Jason Miller/Getty Images LeBron James has paid tribute to former teammate Russell Westbrook – but fans are not buying it. Russell Westbrook announced his retirement from the NBA in the offseason, ending a long career that peaked by winning the MVP in the 2016-17 season. He became the first player to ever average a triple-double for an entire season. Westbrook’s jersey will be retired by the Oklahoma City Thunder, and his former LA Lakers teammate LeBron James has paid tribute to him, speaking to the Mind The Game podcast . James said: “I think one of the things about Russ that doesn’t get talked about is like the guy never wanted to take a night off. Wanted to play in every single game. Being a teammate of his for that year or two, I think it was a year and a half, maybe two years in LA. He never wanted to take a game off. “Never wanted to take a practice off. Great dude. You can never, it’s not going to be one person that played with him in the locker room and he like, man, he wasn’t a good teammate like, everyone raves about him, including myself. “Kudos to him and that jacket, that Hall of Fame jacket is next.” The Lakers traded for Westbrook in 2021, striking a deal with the Wizards in exchange for Kyle Kuzma, Kentavious Caldwell-Pope, Montrezl Harrell, and a 2021 first-round pick. The move was a spectacular failure, with ball-dominant Westbrook and James failing to gel on the court. The Lakers won only 33 games in 2021-22, having lost key depth including Alex Caruso, who was allowed to walk for financial reasons. Frank Vogel was fired and replaced by Darvin Ham, who relegated Westbrook into a bench role. The Lakers eventually traded Westbrook to the Jazz in February 2023. LeBron James slammed for Westbrook comments LeBron James’ tribute to Russell Westbrook has raised eyebrows, after their dysfunctional time on the Lakers together. One fan wrote on social media: “Bron knows deep down he hated playing with him.” A second fan hit out: “LeBron is so fake. He was begging the Lakers to get rid of Russell Westbrook.” Another added: “He just playing it up for the camera, we all know Russ was a locker room vampire.” A third fan noted: “There’s always such an obvious lack of enthusiasm when he talks about Russ.” And another comment added: “Says the dude who used him as a scapegoat.” James eventually moved on from the LA Lakers earlier this year, signing with the Philadelphia 76ers. The 41-year-old appears to be enjoying his basketball a lot more right now than during the Lakers-Westbrook era – which might just have been the least enjoyable from James’ career, at least looking from the outside. item.title: 10 takeaways from Oregon State’s loss at Fresno State
item.description: FRESNO, Calif. — Oregon State lost to Fresno State 38-22 Saturday night at Valley Children’s Stadium. Here are 10 takeaways as the Beavers prepare to host Texas State. 1. Reality check Two things can be true. Oregon State can still be ahead of schedule and on its way to a legitimately surprising season amid a massive rebuild, complete with a potent offense. Much of its success thus far came by pounding less talented teams and several of the worst defenses in the country. And where OSU was vulnerable was there to be exploited by teams like Fresno State, which has talent and good coaching. The Beavers are not a College Football Playoff team. That dose of reality doesn’t diminish what’s being accomplished this season. They’re simply not one of the two most talented teams in the Pac-12 right now. 2. Oregon State was outcoached JaMarcus Shephard and his staff were outcoached for definitely the first time in conference play and arguably for the first time this season. Matt Entz laid out in detail what Fresno State picked up from studying Braden Atkinson from his time at Mercer and Oregon State’s tendencies. Bye weeks also include self-scouting. Fresno State was more prepared for what OSU showed and particularly offensively the Beavers did not have an effective counter. 3. Self-inflicted errors can’t happen in games like this Winning on the road against a team with at least comparable (if not better) talent and coaching is a difficult task to begin with. It becomes a whole lot harder with six presnap penalties and allowing five sacks with two leading to fumbles. OSU absolutely could have led by multiple scores early if not for a false start negating Jake Reichle’s would-be touchdown, if Aeryn Hampton’s foot was in bounds and if multiple other penalties didn’t occur. That doesn’t even get into defensive miscues from missed tackles or over-pursuits. 4. The offensive line may have had its worst game Houston was more physically dominating than Fresno State, but that’s to be expected. Oregon State’s offensive line had a brutal showing nearly across the board, with sacks allowed by multiple players in one-on-one matchups. OSU’s rushing stats are skewed by the sacks and not nearly as poor as the final box score, but the bottom line is Fresno State won the line of scrimmage and it’s not a particularly stout group. 5. Josiah Freeman was the best receiver on the field Fresno State’s 6-foot-4 receiver had a big night with two touchdowns. Freeman had a massive advantage against Isaiah Houi and performed accordingly. If there’s one piece OSU’s receiving corps is missing it is a target with the size and length of Freeman, which the Beavers are leaning on via their tight ends. But an outside target like him is hard to beat and he showed why. 6. Tackling, leverage issues persist OSU showed a vulnerability early, but against Houston and Texas Tech it was understandable in terms of talent and timing on the schedule. item.title: How Oregon State turned a raw athlete into a starting linebacker
item.description: CORVALLIS — Two years ago, Jarrel Comer was a freshman at Tallahassee Community College and had not played competitive football since middle school. Now he’s a starting outside linebacker at Oregon State . Comer played basketball at Eastside High School in Gainesville, Florida, but began college as a regular student. He looked for opportunities to play sports again and football became the opportunity at Citrus College in California. He boarded a plane for the first time to take a cross-country flight to play football for the first time in more than four years. “I was willing to take that chance to get to where I am today,” Comer said. He had 58 tackles (8.5 for loss), including six sacks at the California junior college and got on the radar of linebackers coach Cort Dennison, then at Idaho. Dennison kept pursuing Comer at OSU, where he signed in January and arrived during the spring. Latest Beavers news Justin Joyner wins first game as Oregon State coach in blowout Atkinson, Legree join Nike’s Blue Ribbon Elite as OSU extends apparel deal Pac-12 confirms play clock error led to penalty on Oregon State in its loss to Fresno State At 6-foot-4 and 245 pounds, Comer was dominating in junior college from his athleticism alone. He didn’t know the finer points of playing football. Hand placement, setting the edge in the run game and pass coverage were not in his repertoire. Comer was there to pin his ears back and attack the quarterback, regardless of the down and distance. “They didn’t ask much of me,” Comer said. “They told me just do what I do, use my athleticism, get to the quarterback.” What Comer lacks in experience, he makes up for in ability. He consistently ranks among OSU’s fastest players in practice, which was invaluable to a team seeking more pass rush. “His athleticism is off the charts,” defensive coordinator Mike MacIntyre said. “We see him grow leaps and bounds. Playing a lot more (against Montana), he will grow leaps and bounds going into this Saturday because now he’s seen it, it slows down, he understands the different things.” RELATED: Experts release Oregon State vs. UTEP predictions, best bets, and preview for Week 4 Comer has 10 tackles thus far, including four in each of the past two games, and is already more than a situational pass rusher for the Beavers. He credits MacIntyre and edge coaches Joe Seumalo and George Frazier with helping him learn the game, particularly pass coverage. Ideally, pairing Comer with Takari Hickle will allow OSU to generate more pressure as teams won’t be able to focus all their offensive line on one side. “Teams have to respect his speed,” Hickle said. “If they don’t, then he’ll run right by them. He is definitely a threat in coverage and in the pass game.” Oregon State (1-2) at UTEP (1-2) When: Saturday, Sept. 26 Time: 6 p.m. PT Where: Sun Bowl, El Paso, Texas Betting line: Oregon State by 10.5 TV: MW+ (Mountain West Plus) On air: KEX 1190 in Portland, KEJO 1240 and 93.7 in Corvallis Stream : You c

item.title: Caitlin Clark picks what was ‘the best part’ about the WNBA Finals series
item.description: Photo by Brian Spurlock/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Indiana Fever star Caitlin Clark thinks that the Golden State Valkyries being in the WNBA Finals was the best part of the series. The Valkyries became the first expansion team in American pro sports history to win a championship in their second year. They achieved this feat by beating the Atlanta Dream in a gruelling seven-game series, which they sealed with a 68-63 win in Game 7. Gabby Williams won the Finals MVP award, as she put on a 30-point performance in Game 7. However, the likes of Kiah Stokes and Veronica Burton also played vital roles in helping the Valkyries beat the Dream. While discussing the WNBA Finals, Caitlin Clark offered major praise for how the Valkyries managed to do what many thought was unthinkable. Caitlin Clark praises Golden State Valkyries team chemistry The Valkyries made the playoffs in their very first WNBA season. However, many were not convinced about them, as they felt that the team lacked the star presence that was required to win the WNBA championship. Gabby Williams made sure to bring this point up after the Game 7 win. The togetherness of the team showed that they were ready to do whatever it takes to win, and Clark had nothing but praise for them. “I feel like the best part about the Finals has been that the Valkyries are in it. They’ve been a franchise for two years. I don’t think people realise how ridiculous that is, that they’ve been able to put together a roster and run an organisation as well as they have,” said Clark on Not Gonna Lie with Kylie Kelce. “For Natalie, their coach, to get everybody to buy in, and to get everybody to believe, and they have really talented players but at the same time, on any given night, any of them can have 20 points and be the star. It seems like nobody’s bothered by that, that’s just how they are. They’re a close-knit team. That’s the coolest storyline of the Finals.” No player on the Valkyries roster averaged 15 or more points in the 2026 season. Chicago Sky and Connecticut Sun were the only two teams to have a similar stat. Both of these teams failed to make the playoffs, while the Valkyries marched on to win the championship. The key reason behind this is that all the players on the Valkyries knew their roles and fulfilled them to their best potential. Williams, who was the star of the Finals, had several off games even against the Dream, but other players stepped up and made the difference. Game 5 was a perfect example of that, as Williams struggled and scored 9 points while shooting 3-for-14 from the field. Burton stepped up to add 13 points, 8 rebounds and also had 4 blocks to help the Valkyries get to a 64-55 win. There were multiple games during the season that their bench won them. They had the best bench unit during the regular season, which averaged 34.3 points per game. item.title: TD Cowen: Democratic Congress Would Sink CLARITY Act for Two Years
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine TD Cowen: Democratic Congress Would Sink CLARITY Act for Two Years A Democratic sweep of Congress would end the CLARITY Act’s chances for the next two years and sour the political climate for crypto, TD Cowen’s Washington analyst Jaret Seiberg wrote to Bitcoin Magazine and clients in an election-day note. Seiberg wrote that TD Cowen agrees with polls and prediction markets that Democrats are likely to take both chambers, with the caveat that polls taken a month out, which were more mixed, tend to beat those taken on the eve of a vote. His conclusion for crypto is blunt: “Democrats will likely investigate Trump including his crypto entanglements. We see this as souring the political environment for crypto, which is why we do not expect the Clarity Act to pass over the next two years.” The market structure bill passed the House 294-134 in July 2025 and failed a Senate cloture vote 49-50 on Sept. 15. If it does not pass before the new Congress convenes on Jan. 3, it dies and must be reintroduced. Seiberg added that crypto’s influence may shrink further in Congress if Sherrod Brown wins his Ohio Senate race, a contest the industry spent to lose. In Congress, the Senate is the lever The note treats Senate control as the bigger prize. A Democratic majority could block Trump’s nominees and use that power to force him to fill Democratic seats on the FDIC, SEC and CFTC, the three agencies at the center of crypto policy. It could pressure the White House to drop its effort to remove Lisa Cook from the Federal Reserve board. Trump could answer with acting chiefs, Seiberg wrote, but that risks handing authority to career staff, an outcome “Team Trump” does not want. Senate control would elevate Sen. Elizabeth Warren to chair the Banking Committee. Seiberg sees room for populist bills such as interest rate caps, limits on bank buybacks and a government credit score, and he thinks Warren and Trump could find common ground on some of them. Rep. Maxine Waters would take House Financial Services, with a focus on housing and tighter scrutiny of the FHFA. “That means a focus on housing though we are dubious that she will find GOP support for down payment help and public housing renovations. FHFA scrutiny will increase,” the note read. For banks, the note says the election changes little: regulators will keep easing capital, liquidity and tiering rules whichever party wins. Divided government does raise the odds of a shutdown or a debt-ceiling standoff, since Trump is expected to reject spending conditions Democrats attach. Bitcoin on election day Bitcoin traded near $77,500 Tuesday afternoon eastern time, up from a dip to $76,300 in the morning and about $2,000 below where it opened the month. The price has absorbed a record $6.34 billion Binance hack , two days of spot ETF outflows and a Fed that is leaning toward a December hike. item.title: Goalkeeper Owono breaks down after collision that led to footballer’s death
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye FC Andorra goalkeeper Jesús Owono was reportedly left distraught and broke down in tears in the dressing room after the accidental collision that preceded the death of CD Tenerife forward Jesús de Miguel Alameda, with teammates rallying around him to offer support. According to The Sun UK, the 25-year-old Equatorial Guinea international was seen praying and crying following the incident during Monday’s Segunda División match between Tenerife and Andorra. Owono’s knee struck De Miguel’s head and chest as he rushed out to clear a long ball in the closing stages of the encounter. The 30-year-old striker was left motionless on the pitch, prompting distress among players, some of whom were reportedly seen in tears. The goalkeeper was shown a straight red card before the referee abandoned the match in second-half stoppage time. De Miguel was taken to hospital after reportedly suffering a cardiac arrest on the way, with paramedics said to have resuscitated him. Tenerife initially described his condition as “stable but serious” on Monday night, but he died on Tuesday morning. The Sun, citing Spanish newspaper AS, reported that Andorra players showed great concern for Owono during their journey back from Tenerife, with the goalkeeper visibly shaken by the tragedy. Journalist Ivan Alvarez also told COPE radio that Owono had intended to apologise to De Miguel’s family in person before learning of his death. The goalkeeper has reportedly deactivated his social media accounts since the incident and is said to be seeking an opportunity to offer his condolences to the bereaved family before making a public statement. Meanwhile, a judge is expected to open an investigation into De Miguel’s death, although a Canary Islands court source described the incident as an “accidental collision on the playing field”. The source explained that a judicial investigation is automatically opened in cases of deaths not resulting from natural causes, including accidents. Owono is not expected to face criminal sanctions, according to the report, although he could still face sporting disciplinary action. De Miguel’s partner, Maria, and their one-year-old daughter, Carla, were reportedly watching from the stands when the incident occurred. Tenerife have expressed their grief over the striker’s death, while UEFA has announced that a moment of silence will be observed at all its matches this week in his memory. item.title: DSS DG frees four suspected IPOB members, pays N20m compensation
item.description: The Director-General of the Department of State Services (DGSS), Oluwatosin Adeola Ajayi has set free and approved an initial payment of N20 million to four suspects, out of which, each suspect is to receive five million Naira as compensation after being cleared of alleged membership of the proscribed Indigenous People of Biafra (IPOB). Security sources disclosed that the suspects; Emele Uduma Ibe, Berefgagha Appah, Ondokeyilemi Aggry and Oyeinmokebebeton Aggry, were arrested in May 2022, in Sampou and Akeddei communities in Kolokuma/Opokuma and Sagbama Local Government Areas of Bayelsa State. “The Agency established that they had been misled into believing that they would each receive a monthly payment of N100,000 under the Federal Government’s Amnesty Programme, not knowing that they were being lured by a group of IPOB members who are now facing trial,” disclosed one of the sources. While receiving the four, Deji Adeyanju & Partners, Counsel to the suspects, commended the Service for their relentless efforts towards safeguarding Nigeria’s security, particularly acknowledging the DGSS’ genuine attempt at upholding human rights. Furthermore, he noted the high level of hygiene and professionalism within the Service, being the best he has witnessed in over 20 years of interacting with DSS personnel. He reiterated his earlier public statement that President Tinubu made the right choice in appointing Oluwatosin Adeola Ajayi as DSS DG. Expressing gratitude to the DSS boss, Emele Uduma Ibe who spoke on behalf of others, described the day as the happiest of his life, noting that the experience had taught him a valuable lesson which he would share with others. He offered prayers for God’s continued blessings upon the DSS boss and the management of the Service. Recall that upon assuming office in 2024, the DG ordered a review of over 300 inherited terrorism cases. Currently, the DSS panel has been able to decongest its facility to about 100 after thorough investigations, paying over a billion naira in compensation. The DSS boss awarded N20 million and covered the medical bills of a Jos based businessman, who was shot erroneously by service personnel in Plateau State. Chineze Ozoadibe was also compensated with N10 million after she was wrongfully arrested, Sunday Ifedi who was also compensated with 10 million naira after investigation cleared him of ties with IPOB, likewise Kenneth Okechukwu Nwafor was also paid N5 million after investigation absolved him of IPOB allegations. item.title: 2027: Why youth share of voters dropped – INEC
item.description: ….As UniJos wins campus debate finale By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA: The Independent National Electoral Commission INEC has explained why youths now make up 29.79 per cent of the voters’ register being prepared for the 2027 general election, down from 39.65 per cent in the 2023 register. Chairman of the commission, Prof. Joash Amupitan SAN, gave the explanation on Tuesday at the grand finale of the INEC Campus Debate at the Law Theatre of the University of Abuja. He said the drop does not mean fewer young people are interested in elections, but that many who counted as youths in 2023 have simply grown older. “Some questions have been asked, why has the number reduced compared to what we have in 2023? But the truth of the matter is that there has been progressive migration of the categories of persons that were youth in 2023, they have now migrated into different age groups”, Amupitan explained. He said the register, “which is currently being reviewed through claims and objection,” puts youth representation at 29.79 per cent. The 2023 register had 37,060,399 youths aged 18 to 34, or 39.65 per cent of the 93.4 million registered voters. Amupitan said the debate was part of the commission’s effort to confront voter apathy among young people. “Our plan is to catch them young,” he said. He said earlier outings showed how little many young people know about the electoral process. “When they ask who is the INEC chairman, unfortunately none of them could get it,” he said. The University of Jos won the final, which was held under the theme “Nigeria’s Electoral Process and Democracy.” Bayero University, Kano, came second, the University of Ibadan third, and the University of Nigeria, Nsukka, fourth. Amupitan, who is a University of Jos alumnus, said the judges’ decision could not be faulted. “From the quality of the debate, it was, honestly, it could go either way and they have done justice to it,” he said. He said the judges took a long time to compute the scores. “They were also trying to use technology with their phone making some computations and arithmetics just to ensure that there is accurate delivery,” he said. Amupitan said the result was so clear that no debater or university should think of going to court. “It will be needless for any of the parties or debaters to think of going to court. So that is why we are not establishing any election petition, any tribunal to review what has been done,” he said light-heartedly. He also told the Director of Voter Education and Publicity to keep track of the finalists, saying he would have employed them immediately if the law allowed. “They are not qualified to have been given automatic employment, if not I will have done that by now,” he said. He added that they must first graduate and complete the National Youth Service Corps NYSC. item.title: Police uncover fake dollar operation in Ondo, arrest suspect
item.description: By Dayo Johnson, Akure The Ondo State Police Command has uncovered a suspected counterfeit dollar printing operation in Odigbo Local Government Area, arresting one suspect and recovering three bags of suspected fake United States dollar notes. The operation followed an investigation into an alleged $6,000 currency fraud involving a businessman in Okitipupa. The police said the case began after Yusuf Nasiru, of Sabo, Okitipupa, lodged a complaint on October 28, 2026, alleging that two men, Peter Desmond and Olami Toro, both from Ode-Irele, approached him at his shop on October 25 to exchange dollars for naira. According to the complainant, he handed over $6,000, valued at about N8.6 million, to the men. However, while waiting for the naira equivalent, the suspects allegedly returned the dollars, claiming they did not have enough money to complete the transaction, before leaving. Nasiru later discovered that the returned notes were counterfeit and reported the matter to the police. The Police Public Relations Officer, DSP Jimoh Abayomi, said operatives of the Okitipupa Division commenced an investigation following receipt of the complaint. He said intelligence gathering and technical tracking led the operatives to one of the suspects, Peter Desmond, at Kiniso Village, via Ajue, in Odigbo LGA. “Acting on credible intelligence from community members, operatives raided the hideout on October 29, 2026, believed to be used for producing and printing counterfeit dollar notes to defraud unsuspecting members of the public,” Abayomi said. He disclosed that one suspect was arrested during the raid, while other occupants of the premises escaped through a perimeter fence. A search of the premises, he said, led to the recovery of three bags containing suspected counterfeit US dollar notes and a small wooden box, which had been taken into police custody as exhibits. Abayomi added that the arrested suspect had provided useful information to assist the ongoing investigation. He said the Commissioner of Police, Felix Ohagwu, had directed that the investigation be intensified to apprehend other suspects, establish the full extent of the alleged criminal network and prosecute those found culpable. The command cautioned residents against engaging in suspicious foreign currency transactions with unverified individuals or accepting seemingly attractive exchange offers outside authorised channels. It also advised members of the public to authenticate foreign currencies before accepting them and report suspicious activities to the nearest police station. The police assured residents of their commitment to combating financial crimes and protecting lives and property across the state. The post Police uncover fake dollar operation in Ondo, arrest suspect appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Nigeria’s exports rise 25% in two years — NPA
item.description: By Godwin Oritse The Nigerian Ports Authority (NPA) has said the country’s exports increased by more than 25 per cent in the last two years, attributing the growth to Federal Government reforms and improved collaboration with port operators. The Managing Director of NPA, Dr Abubakar Dantsoho, disclosed this while speaking at the ongoing Annual World Ports Conference in London, organised by the International Association of Ports and Harbours (IAPH). He said Nigeria’s population and economic potential gave it an advantage over other countries in West and Central Africa, adding that recent reforms had also improved cargo throughput at the nation’s ports. Dantsoho said the export growth was not limited to oil and gas but extended to manufacturing and agricultural products, including cocoa, cashew and other raw materials. “Statistically, the exports from Nigeria in the last two years has increased by 25 per cent. And then these are exports that are not mainly only oil and gas. In terms of oil and gas, like I mentioned, we are doing fantastically around that, but then also in the other areas of manufacturing and agriculture, you know, raw materials like cocoa, like cashew and all that. Volumes have increased,” he said. He attributed the growth partly to the partnership between the NPA and major terminal operators, particularly APM Terminals. The NPA chief said the authority had put measures in place to sustain the growth, including the establishment of Export Processing Terminals to facilitate the handling and documentation of export cargoes. He disclosed that about four such terminals were operating in Nigeria, with the NPA collaborating with terminal operators, the Nigeria Customs Service and other relevant agencies to ensure that export cargoes were processed locally and met required standards before shipment. Dantsoho said the reforms had also positioned Nigeria to take greater advantage of the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA), particularly through increased trade with other African countries. He cited Nigeria’s engagement with Morocco, which he described as a growing manufacturing hub for electric and other vehicles, as an example of opportunities for cooperation. The NPA managing director also attributed Nigeria’s improved performance in global port rankings to increased efficiency, technology adoption and collaboration with industry stakeholders. He said two Nigerian ports featured among the top 20 in the latest World Bank global ports ranking. Dantsoho further disclosed that revenue generated from ports across the country had quadrupled, alongside an increase in cargo volumes. He said the authority was monitoring port performance across West and Central Africa through a regional dashboard, adding that the data showed improvements in Nigeria’s port efficiency as well as progress in countries such as Tanzania and Kenya. item.title: Google dismantles botnet secretly running on 1.3 million Android TV boxes
item.description: Google's Threat Intelligence Group says it has shut down a massive botnet called x.cpe. At its height, x.cpe ran on more than 1.3 million Android TV devices, and unusually, these were Google-certified boxes. Google says its screening process missed the malware due to "obfuscation techniques" employed by Shenzhen-based Videostrong Technology. In a detailed blog post , the Threat Intelligence Group explains how the x.cpe botnet evolved quickly from a single-stage dropper into a modular three-stage malware platform that sold access to third parties. Manufacturers must have their devices certified if they want access to Google apps and branding, a process that is supposed to catch threats like this. However, Videostrong's compromised boxes, mostly sold under the MECOOL brand, evaded detection by using a backdoor to remotely install the malware after the devices were set up and online. After devices appeared online, a stub application called x.cpe or com.oemservice would phone home. This package did not have any malicious capabilities of its own, but it had the system-level permissions necessary to install malware modules at the operator's behest. It also disabled Play Protect, which would have otherwise flagged the silently installed packages as malicious. Read full article Comments

item.title: Ondo Amotekun arrests 301 suspects, deploys 1,200 officers
item.description: By Dayo Johnson, Akure The Ondo State Security Network Agency, codenamed Amotekun, says it arrested 301 suspected kidnappers and other criminals between August and October 2026. The State Commander, Chief Adetunji Adeleye, disclosed this while parading 15 suspects, including those allegedly involved in the abduction of a poultry farmer, Afolabi Ajayi, in Imafon community, Akure North Local Government Area, and the killing of a woman. Adeleye also announced the launch of Operation Laafia DanDan, a security initiative aimed at tackling criminal activities during the ember months and yuletide. He said the corps had secured the conviction of 27 suspects, who were either serving various jail terms or fulfilling conditions attached to options of fines. “Across the board, within these months under review, we arrested 301 suspects. Out of these 301 suspects, we have secured conviction of 27 serving various jail terms or fulfilling conditions for those that have option of fine. “Using alternative dispute resolution on many cases, we were able to resolve 102 cases,” he said. Adeleye attributed the achievements to the support of Amotekun ambassadors across the 18 local government areas, intelligence officers, local task forces, vigilantes and personnel of the corps. He said the agency was winding down its previous operation to begin full deployment for the ember months, with intelligence-led surveillance across the state, particularly on major highways, in urban centres and forest reserves. According to him, the new operation will feature increased patrols by Amotekun Rangers in forests, as well as electronic and physical monitoring of identified crime-prone locations. “We have redesigned a scheme whereby we will have a different operation for this period to guarantee safety of lives and property in Ondo State and for those commuting. “We want to reassure the public that the state remains safe as we are determined to continue 24/7 patrol across all major roads, forest reserves and the metropolis,” he said. The commander disclosed that about 1,200 personnel would be deployed across the 18 local government areas, with particular attention to border communities and routes. He also presented a kidnap victim who was recently rescued without payment of ransom. Adeleye said the corps had commenced training and retraining of personnel on arrest procedures and prosecution, adding that suspects whose investigations had been concluded would be charged to court. On the 15 suspects paraded, he said four were arrested for alleged violations of the state’s anti-grazing law, two for breach of law and order, while nine were arrested in connection with kidnapping. He said three suspects linked to the abduction of poultry farmer Ajayi and the killing of the woman had been arrested, adding that they were identified by the victim and had allegedly confessed to the offences. item.title: Okorocha to Uzodimma: Stop insulting judges, appeal up to the Supreme Court
item.description: By Ikechukwu Nnochiri ABUJA — A former governor of Imo State, Rochas Okorocha, whom the court recently declared the authentic candidate of the All Progressives Congress (APC) for the 2027 senatorial election in Imo West, has warned his successor, Governor Hope Uzodimma, to stop what he described as unwarranted attacks on judges. Okorocha, who spoke at the Federal High Court premises in Abuja after signing processes at the registry in connection with the ongoing legal dispute over the senatorial ticket, urged Governor Uzodimma to exercise his right of appeal, even up to the Supreme Court. He also called on the governor to restrain his supporters, whom he accused of continuing to denigrate the judiciary over a lost case. He said: “I listened to the news yesterday and it was so horrible, so terrible, that Governor Hope’s aides, namely his Deputy Chief of Staff and the National Vice Chairman of the APC, could berate a judge, insult a judge. “To use his words, he said the judgment was rubbish and procured, and that the judge should go and look at himself in the mirror. I think that is terrible. And the other one, who is called his Deputy Chief of Staff and whose wife is even a judge, could be insulting the judge because of a judgment. “So, it means that whenever the judgment is for Hope, it is good, but whenever it is against him, the Judiciary is evil. “I think this is very uncivilized. I want him to caution his attack dogs and his people to refrain from insulting judges. It doesn’t represent this nation well, and I feel particularly hurt. “I was made to understand that he has called all his aides, commissioners and everybody to go on the attack. You see, they are doing all that. Can’t he wait patiently and try to get the appeal through? At least the Supreme Court is there. “So it is very shocking and very surprising. I don’t know what they expected: that the judge should have said that the election was held on the 16th for Hope, when the actual date is the 18th? “Or that he would have said that Hope emerged by consensus, which is not true? Or the paper signed only by the Resident Electoral Commissioner (REC) of Imo State and sent to the National Chairman, saying that it was by consensus and that Hope’s election took place two days before the time? “I don’t understand what their quarrel is all about. I want to say once more: let us protect the sanctity of the Judiciary and let us allow justice to prevail in all matters. Hope has been a very big and unusual beneficiary of the court, and I think he should have respected it.” Okorocha challenged Uzodimma to fault his claims in public rather than attacking judges and the Judiciary, adding: “If you (Uzodimma) think any of the things I am saying is not true and that the judgment is not true, Hope should come on television or come and speak. “Why is he (Uzodimma) hiding and using attack dogs here and there to attack judges? item.title: Hubble Telescope sees cosmic 'cat's tail' that could wrap around Earth and the sun 500 times
item.description: null Using the Hubble Space Telescope, astronomers have investigated a cosmic cat's tail, finding it likely formed after two Pluto-sized bodies smashed together. The feature, nicknamed the Cat's Tail, extends out from the debris disk known as Beta Pictoris which is located in a planetary system located 63 light-years away. This tail would put that of the average tabby to shame: It's so long that it could curl around the sun-Earth system about 500 times. That's about as long as 200 trillion house cats. The major difference between our solar system and the planetary system that hosts the Cat's Tail is the latter's relative youth. While our solar system is around 4.6 billion years old , Beta Pictoris is a cosmic kitten no more than a few million years old. That means it is still host to collisions between planetary bodies similar to the ones that rocked the solar system during its infancy. The team behind this research gained new insights into the Cat's Tail using 14 years of observations. This allowed them to solve the long-standing mystery of the violent conditions under which it formed. "The Cat's Tail is thought to be the aftermath of a collision between large bodies — think something like Pluto ," team leader Arin Avsar of the University of Arizona said in a statement. "Oddly, this feature had previously only been seen with the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST), which detects infrared light, but remained invisible at shorter wavelengths, which has puzzled the community for a while." Cosmic cat tail is also pleasingly fluffy Comparing Beta Pictoris and our solar system, one thing rapidly becomes apparent: our cosmic neighborhood is relatively well-ordered. The planets orbit the sun with most space rocks neatly delegated into bands: the main asteroid belt between Mars and Jupiter , and the Kuiper belt out beyond the orbit of Neptune. However, this is a stark contrast to the solar system's violent and chaotic youth. Back then, the solar system was host to an infant star surrounded by a swirling disk of gas and dust in which collisions between bodies called planetesimals — the building blocks of planets — were commonplace. Astronomers can't look back to the solar system's infancy, so to learn more about how our cosmic backyard took shape, they study nearby young planetary systems. Systems like Beta Pictoris. That doesn't mean it has been quick to divulge its secrets, though. "We think the Cat's Tail has eluded our observations in visible light until now because of what it's made of," Avsar explained. "It consists almost entirely of what we call organic refractory material, which is heavily carbon-based. These long chains of carbon atoms absorb visible light, so they're quite black." This new study revealed that the feline feature is cat-like in more ways than just its shape. It's also pleasingly fluffy, Hubble observations suggest. item.title: Farmers-herders clashes reduced in Kano — Commissioner
item.description: By Hadiza Yusuf The Kano State Government says clashes between farmers and herders have reduced significantly following the demarcation of 1,270 kilometres of cattle routes across the state. The Commissioner for Agriculture and Natural Resources, Dr Danjuma Mahmoud, disclosed this on Tuesday while outlining the achievements of the ministry. He said the demarcation had helped address recurring disputes between farmers and herders by providing designated routes for the movement of livestock. According to him, the initiative formed part of the state government’s efforts to tackle longstanding challenges in the agricultural sector and promote peaceful coexistence between farming and pastoral communities. “One important problem that I want to reiterate is the intractable problem of clashes between farmers and herders. We have made significant progress in that regard. “Our project provided demarcated cattle routes covering about 1,270 kilometres across the state. That is why you now hear that clashes between herders and farmers have reduced to the barest minimum in Kano State,” he said. Mahmoud said the ministry had also implemented interventions to boost agricultural production, including the rehabilitation of irrigation facilities and the expansion of cultivable farmland. He disclosed that more than 1,200 acres of farmland had been recovered through the clearing of irrigation channels and rehabilitation of canals at major irrigation sites. The commissioner added that the state government, in collaboration with the African Development Bank-supported Agricultural Transformation Agenda Support Programme (ATASP), had recovered more than 200 additional acres for irrigation. He said the government had secured approval to develop 11 mini dams and irrigation facilities across 11 local government areas. “When completed, these projects will provide about 2,000 additional acres of irrigable farmland in the state,” he said. Mahmoud further disclosed that the ministry had completed more than 70 milk collection centres to improve milk handling and storage in pastoral communities. He said the centres were equipped with storage facilities and solar-powered cooling systems to preserve milk before transportation to markets. The post Farmers-herders clashes reduced in Kano — Commissioner appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Insecurity: Borno Police nab 103 suspected criminals
item.description: By Ndahi Marama, Maiduguri The Borno State Police Command has arrested 103 suspected criminals in connection to combat substance abuse, violence, thuggery and other social vices. The arrests were carried out in Maiduguri metropolis between the months of October 29 to November 2nd, 2026, with support from its Rapid Response Squad (RRS) – Social Vices Unit. This was disclosed by the Police Public Relations Officer, ASP Keneth Daso in a statement he signed on Tuesday. The statement reads partly: “In a sustained effort to rid Maiduguri metropolis of criminal elements and combat substance abuse, violence, thuggery and other social vices, the Borno State Police Command, through its Rapid Response Squad (RRS) – Social Vices Unit, has recorded a major operational breakthrough with the arrest of 103 suspects during a week-long township patrol and coordinated raid operations conducted between 29th October and 2nd November 2026. “The operations, carried out on the directives of the Commissioner of Police, CP Naziru Abdulmajid, psc, involved a combined team of Police operatives and other relevant security agencies. “The joint operations focused on identified crime-prone areas and security hotspots across the metropolis, including Gwange, Santiago, Texaco, Ajari, Gadan Zare, Budum, Shehuri, Bulabulin, Abbaganaram, Baga Road, Gidan Dambe, UNIMAID 202 Housing Estate, Mairi Kuwait, Bakari, Zanneri, Polo, Giwa Barrack Area, Kwanan Yobe, Jiddari, Kaleri, Damboa Road, Circular and Moduganari, among other locations. “The operations resulted in the arrest of 103 suspects for offences bordering on public nuisance, possession and sale of illicit drugs, and possession of dangerous weapons. “The suspects are undergoing preliminary screening and investigation, while those found culpable will be prosecuted in accordance with the law”. Daso said. Items recovered include; 889 wraps of Indian hemp, 104 wraps of Erinmo, 7 packs of Colorado and 2 quantities of methamphetamine (Ice). Also recovered according to the statement are 8 bottles of Codeine syrup, 266 tablets of D5, 13 tablets of Diazepam, 11 tablets of Tramadol, 7 capsules of Tramadol and 300 capsules of Exole. Additionally Daso said, 12 tablets of Exole, 4 ice bunkers, 1 bottle of Methylene Chloride, popularly known as “Suck and Die”, 4 sharp knives, 1 cutlass. 16. 1 axe, 11 rounds of live ammunition, 3 sets of Shisha pots and 11 pieces of ice bulbs were recovered from the suspects. “The Commissioner of Police, CP Naziru Abdulmajid, psc, commended the operatives and collaborating security agencies for their commitment, vigilance and proactive approach to maintaining public safety. “He reaffirmed the Command’s resolve to sustain intelligence-led operations, intensify the fight against illicit drug activities and dismantle criminal hideouts and networks capable of threatening public peace and security. “The Command calls on members of the public to sustain their cooperation with security agencies by providing credible a

item.title: This space company is betting its future on a propellant available everywhere
item.description: Robert, Ryan, and Kirby Carlisle are three engineers who worked at SpaceX during the Falcon 9 era, seeing the revolution in the global launch industry from the inside. The brothers launched rockets, refurbished rockets, and sold rockets. But when it came time for them to leave SpaceX and start their own space company—a lifetime dream for the Carlisle brothers—they chose not to build rockets. Rather, they focused on spacecraft. In late 2022, the three Carlisles founded Argo Space to build infrastructure in space. Their vision was not just in-space transportation but also removing the need to use propellants from Earth to move around the heavens. item.title: EFCC Uncovers Chinese-Operated Illegal Oil Refinery In Ogun
item.description: The Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) says it has uncovered an illegal oil refinery allegedly operated by Chinese nationals in the Ogere area of Ogun State. The Commission disclosed that the operation, carried out on Saturday, October 31, 2026, by operatives of its Lagos Zonal Directorate 2, followed intelligence gathering and surveillance on the activities of illegal sludge oil refiners. The development was contained in a statement issued on Tuesday by the EFCC Head of Media and Publicity, Dele Oyewale. The illegal oil refinery allegedly operated by Chinese nationals. X/@officialEFCC According to the Commission, the refinery was deserted when operatives stormed the premises, following an earlier crackdown on four illegal lithium processing plants in the area. However, they discovered waste products from the refining process, as well as underground tanks believed to have been used for heating and processing sludge oil. “Two of the underground tanks inspected contained substances suspected to be Automotive Gas Oil (AGO), otherwise known as diesel,” the statement said. The EFCC said preliminary investigations showed that the operators sourced sludge oil, also known as black sludge, from Warri in Delta State and Port Harcourt in Rivers State before transporting it to the facility in Ogere for processing. The illegal oil refinery allegedly operated by Chinese nationals. X/@officialEFCC It explained that further investigations indicated that the operators subjected the sludge oil to intense heat, allowing lighter petroleum components to pass through a series of chambers and filters in a process believed to produce Automotive Gas Oil (AGO) for sale in the Nigerian market. The Commission added that security personnel at the facility told its operatives that the Chinese operators never disclosed their identities or the name of the company behind the operation. Operatives of the Lagos Zonal Directorate 2 have since taken over the premises as investigations continue to establish the identities of the operators, ownership of the facility and the full extent of the suspected illegal activities and economic sabotage. The post EFCC Uncovers Chinese-Operated Illegal Oil Refinery In Ogun appeared first on Channels Television .

item.title: Binance Says $6.34 Billion Hack Began With Fake Job Interview
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Binance Says $6.34 Billion Hack Began With Fake Job Interview The $6.34 billion theft from Binance began with a fake job interview and ran for five months before a single coin moved, the exchange said Tuesday in its first public account of the Oct. 29 attack. Another initial incident report from Binance, released alongside a media briefing by co-CEO Richard Teng and chief security officer Jimmy Su, describes a campaign that combined a poisoned software download, a staged recruitment process, malware that evaded endpoint detection and an internal AI tool the attackers turned against the company’s own wallet engineers. Binance said it has frozen or intercepted about $2.85 billion of the stolen assets and replenished 98% of affected tokens from its own funds, with the balance being bought on the open market. “This wasn’t one mistake or one breach — it was a months-long campaign,” Teng wrote on X. “We’re publishing the full report because the lessons go far beyond Binance.” The FBI has attributed the attack to North Korea. Binance’s report cites that finding but stops short of its own attribution. Pyongyang rejected the claim Monday, with Kim Yo Jong, sister of leader Kim Jong Un, calling it a “grave political provocation” through state media. The Binance hack had five months of preparation According to Binance, the first foothold for this hack came in June. A wallet DevOps engineer searched for a popular AI coding tool and downloaded a tampered Homebrew installer. Binance’s security team caught the anomaly, replaced the device and rotated credentials, but the episode exposed the engineer’s role and the names of colleagues on the wallet infrastructure team. In September, a second engineer was approached on a legitimate job platform by someone posing as a project director. A video interview with a purported HR representative followed, with the interviewer sharing a personal social media account to build trust. A second interview with a supposed CEO ended with an “assignment”: a code repository the engineer was told to install on his work machine. The repository replaced a legitimate pyenv component with a malicious version and opened a channel to an attacker-controlled server. Binance said the zero-day malware was not flagged by its endpoint tools at the time. On Oct. 20, the attackers used that machine and an internal AI tool to reach two more wallet engineers, one of whom held a container deployment token. On Oct. 29, between 17:15 and 19:56 UTC, they logged into a third engineer’s computer, deployed a container with the stolen credentials and launched the drain. Binance said it blocked 57 other suspected North Korea-linked attempts this year using similar lures. Four hours to contain The money left fast. Between 20:05 and 20:09 UTC, five hot wallets sent 233.46 million XRP to an attacker address. Wallets on Solana and Optimism followed with about 970,500 SOL and 44.2 million OP. A Binance hot wallet then sent 18,270 BTC. The attack

item.title: Password manager mSecure tells users to change passwords, won't say why
item.description: Password manager mSecure has warned customers to change their passwords, reset two-factor authentication, and potentially remove their passkeys after detecting suspicious activity, but it has not explained what happened or whether anyone's secrets were exposed. In an email sent to customers on November 3, seen by The Register , US-based developer mSeven Software said it launched an investigation after discovering something amiss with its password management application. "mSeven Software ('mSeven') recently learned of suspicious activity associated with the mSecure password management application," the company wrote. "In response, mSeven quickly launched an investigation, took steps to mitigate the issue, and engaged external cybersecurity experts to assist." The company has yet to answer what the suspicious activity involved, when it occurred, or whether attackers accessed customer information. Its advice to customers, however, suggests that they should take this seriously. "Given the potential security implications, mSeven recommends that you immediately take steps to protect all confidential information stored within the mSecure password management application," the email continued. "This may include changing passwords, resetting or re-enrolling two-factor authentication methods, or removing existing passkeys." For anyone with hundreds of passwords stored in mSecure, that's potentially hours of work. And without knowing what happened, customers have no way of telling which credentials they actually need to replace. The warning has understandably gone down poorly with customers, who have taken to mSecure's support forum demanding answers. "Please provide more context to your email below advising there has been a security breach," one customer wrote. "It is not acceptable to offer the vague advice 'take steps'. Please state what remedial action is required, and what data was compromised." Others are wondering whether they're expected to spend the next several days changing every password they've ever saved. "I have over 800 passwords in mSecure, is the email saying I need to change all of them!" another customer asked. A separate user, who said they had more than 500 passwords stored in the application, questioned whether the warning applied to every two-factor authentication method and passkey associated with their accounts, or just those used to access mSecure itself. The confusion has also spilled onto Reddit , where customers have shared copies of the vague notification and questioned what might have happened. mSeven has yet to respond to The Register 's questions, leaving customers to guess whether their data has actually been compromised or the company is simply being cautious. That's not exactly reassuring from a business whose entire purpose is keeping other people's secrets safe. The company's email concludes: "We regret any inconvenience that this may cause." For Heye, Donald Trump's greatest political vulnerability may lie in the widening gap between his rhetoric of economic success and voters' everyday financial anxieties. item.title: UEFI bootkit infected fully patched Windows machines. Is Microsoft to blame?
item.description: In 2023, malware tracked as BlackLotus became the first publicly documented in-the-wild UEFI bootkit capable of bypassing Secure Boot on fully updated Windows 11 systems. With the industry-wide chain-of-trust mechanism subverted, the malware was able to run malicious code before Windows was fully loaded and many security defenses were operational. Microsoft had already patched the vulnerability that BlackLotus exploited in 2022. In 2023 and 2024, Microsoft issued additional updates. The first added a new certificate that no longer trusted the vulnerable boot managers. The second provided the means to revoke trust in the digital certificate used to sign older vulnerable Windows boot managers. The organizations infected by the new bootkit, which is tracked under the name BlackX, had installed all of these patches. So how did they fall victim? UEFI bootkit refresher Before discussing the incident further, a brief review of BlackLotus and UEFI malware is in order. Short for Unified Extensible Firmware Interface , UEFI is firmware that runs immediately after a computer is turned on. One of its main jobs is to load system configuration settings, identify and initialize hardware components, and prepare the computer to start its OS. Read full article Comments

item.title: GhostBSD 26.2 takes the fright out of FreeBSD with a friendlier installer
item.description: GhostBSD, the easiest-to-install flavor of FreeBSD for the daemon-curious desktop dabbler, is back with a fresh update. GhostBSD 26.2-R15.1p6 , to give it its slightly unwieldy full version number, is based on FreeBSD 15.1. It brings a new installer, full-disk encryption support, a smaller installation image, and fixes across its desktop tools. FreeBSD 15.1 was released back in June , and at the time of writing, it's the most recent point release of FreeBSD. The original plan was that FreeBSD 15.1 would include the option of installing KDE Plasma directly from the setup program, so that the OS would have a graphical desktop from its very first boot. However, this feature isn't ready just yet. That gap inspired Daemonarchy, which we covered late last month . But its Omarchy-derived, keyboard-driven tiling desktop can feel unfamiliar even to experienced Linux users accustomed to conventional desktops. GhostBSD has different goals. It brings Linux-like desktop convenience to FreeBSD: a live graphical environment to explore before installation, a graphical installer, and tools for managing software and updates. These conveniences are familiar to desktop Linux users, but a standard FreeBSD installation takes more work. Its text-mode installer leaves users to install and configure a graphical desktop themselves, if they want one. This is just how the BSD family does things, and most BSD users we've talked to regard it as standard operating procedure and see nothing wrong with it. For Linux users who are curious about how things are on the other side of the FOSS Unix fence, though, those extra steps can form formidable barriers. GhostBSD is an attempt to lay down a welcome mat. The standard edition of GhostBSD installs the MATE desktop, and the downloads page also offers a community-maintained version with Xfce instead. As the project said it would back in February, this release uses the XLibre fork of the X.org X11 server. That's one fewer desktop than when we last tried GhostBSD in August 2025 . That release also offered the Mac OS X-like Gershwin environment. There are practical hardware fixes too. The release notes list improvements for Intel AX200 Wi-Fi cards, open networks, password alerts, and non-ASCII network names, while USB HID support is enabled by default. Where has Gershwin gone? Gershwin remains in active development , so we asked project lead Joe Maloney why it wasn't included. "It has been difficult to find time to package for GhostBSD. It's the only distro I have ever packaged for," Maloney said. He added that rapid contributions from AppImage creator Simon Peter, known as probono, had made packaging increasingly difficult. He also pointed to the fact that GhostBSD project lead Eric Turgeon is developing his own environment too: the Mocka desktop . Mocka is still in its very early stages – alpha version 0.0.2 appeared early last month – but the plan is that when it's ready, it will become GhostBSD's default desktop. For now, the only a

item.title: Pan-African School Games 2026: Celebrating Young Talent, School Pride and New Opportunities
item.description: The Pan-African School Games 2026 brought together young athletes from schools across Lagos for three days of swimming, athletics and football, celebrating sporting talent, school pride and the opportunities that organized competition can create for children and young people. Held at James Hope College, Lekki, from 16 to 18 October, the second edition of the Games featured the U-11, U-13 and U-15 categories. Students competed for individual honours and school points while gaining valuable experience in a structured, multi-sport environment. The competition also welcomed sporting stakeholders and scouts, reinforcing the wider ambition of the Pan-African School Games: to give young athletes a platform where their abilities can be demonstrated, recognized and developed. Building on the Inaugural Games The second edition of the Pan-African School Games built on the foundation established by the inaugural Games in 2025, continuing the vision of creating meaningful sporting opportunities for young athletes. The 2026 edition welcomed schools and student-athletes for three days of swimming, athletics and football, providing a platform for competition, talent development and school pride. Beyond the sporting results, the Games continued to advance a broader ambition: to connect schools, athletes, sporting stakeholders and educational institutions while creating opportunities for young people to develop their abilities and explore future pathways through sport. Day One: Swimming Opens the Games Swimming opened the competition, bringing young swimmers together for races across the U-11, U-13 and U-15 categories. The opening day set the pace for the Games as athletes took to the pool to test their abilities, pursue strong performances and earn points for their schools. The races highlighted the preparation, discipline and technique required to compete, while providing young swimmers with valuable experience in a formal sporting environment. For many of the students, the opportunity to compete alongside athletes from other schools added to the significance of the experience. Each race contributed to the overall competition, with schools beginning their campaigns for medals and category honours. Day Two: Athletics Puts Young Athletes to the Test Athletics took centre stage on the second day, with track and field events testing the speed, strength, coordination and technique of the young competitors. Athletes competed in running, jumping and throwing events, earning points for their schools as the standings developed. Each discipline presented a different challenge, giving students opportunities to demonstrate their abilities and compete for individual and team honours. The athletics programme added another dimension to the Games, highlighting the variety of talent within the participating schools and the value of giving young athletes opportunities to develop through competition. item.title: The Star Wars Eclipse — Want to see the 2027 total solar eclipse on Tatooine? Head to Tunisia
item.description: null On Aug. 2, 2027, darkness will fall on Tatooine. The path of the " eclipse of the century" crosses southern Tunisia, putting several of the most famous Star Wars filming locations in the moon's shadow for up to four minutes. Around Tozeur, eclipse chasers can experience totality among the dunes of Mos Espa and the rocky Jundland Wastes, while on Djerba, locations used for Mos Eisley and Obi-Wan Kenobi's home will also briefly go dark. Other iconic sites are tantalizingly close to — but beyond — the southern edge of the path of totality. For example, Hotel Sidi Idriss , used as Lars Homestead in the original movie and in Attack of the Clones , gets only a 99.98% partial eclipse. So too Chott el-Djerid , site of the famous "binary" sunset over the salt flats — let's hope someone gets a partial eclipse shot from this iconic site. The nearby real-life Tunisian town of Tataouine is also just outside of the path. For Star Wars fans planning to chase the 2027 eclipse, location will be everything. Here are four filming locations firmly inside the path of totality. All times, totality durations and historical cloud cover data come from Time and Date . 1. Eriguet dunes (Mos Espa) Built for Star Wars: Episode I — The Phantom Menace , the Mos Espa film set in the Tunisian desert. (Image credit: Chiara Salvadori via Getty Images) Location: south of Chott el-Gharsa, Tozeur Governorate, southwest Tunisia Start of totality and duration: 10:06 a.m. CET; 2 minutes, 9 seconds Chance of clouds: 2% With a massive budget and three prequels to make, Lucasfilm built a new film set that would double as the Mos Espa spaceport on Tatooine for The Phantom Menace and Attack of the Clones . This is where Qui-Gon Jinn, Obi-Wan Kenobi, Jar Jar Binks and Padme get stranded, where they meet Anakin Skywalker and where the podrace takes place. Now abandoned , it's in the middle of nowhere, between two huge salt lakes and subject to the intense heat and moving Eriguet dunes — but it is firmly within the path of totality. Nearby are two other shooting locations — the Ong Jemel outcrop , where Darth Maul arrives on the scene, and Yardang , where Qui-Gon and Darth Maul battle — the first-ever lightsaber duel filmed on location. 2. Maguer Gorge (Jundland Wastes) Tourists enjoy sunset at Onk Jemal, the desert location of "Star Wars" movies. (Image credit: Maremagnum via Getty Images) Location: Jebel Sidi Bouhlel canyon, Dghoumès National Park, Tozeur, southwest Tunisia Start of totality and duration: 10:06 a.m. CET; 3 minutes, 37 seconds Chance of clouds: 1% Often called "Star Wars Canyon" by fans and crew, Maguer Gorge in Jebel Sidi Bouhlel doubled as the Jundland Wastes of Tatooine in Star Wars: Episode IV — A New Hope . It's where Luke Skywalker is attacked by Tusken Raiders, where Obi-Wan Kenobi first appears and where Luke and Obi-Wan discover the slaughtered Jawas.
